title: 2028 Mercedes-Benz VLE-Class First Drive: Don't Call It a Minivan
text:
Those who resided in New York City or any of the nation's population-dense metropolitan environments around the turn of the millennium probably remember the transformation: Seemingly overnight, the time-tested four-door sedan limousine disappeared from the urban landscape, replaced by full-size SUVs as the luxury transport vehicle of choice for upscale car services. With their spacious interiors, their sturdy truck-based chassis (better suited for navigating aging infrastructure), and automakers' collective decision to cull the herd of suitable sedans, it seemed the natural selection of evolution was at work.
Now, two and a half decades into the 21st century, Mercedes-Benz is attempting to kick-start a similar regime change with its new VLE-class van, an electric vehicle aimed straight at the heart of the VIP car-service industry.
Mercedes is convinced that the VLE-class passenger vehicle—staffers repeatedly insisted that it's not a "van," mini or otherwise—is a cut above any current minivans that lean into the luxury segment. So much so that Mercedes executives use the phrase "Grand Limousine" for the luxury-focused versions of the VLE. One executive told us the brand's U.S. dealer network thinks "minivan" is a bad word.   
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2028 Mercedes-Benz VLE-class EV for sale near 534236
A Low-Flying Private Jet on Wheels with a World-Class Cinema
Though luxury versions of the full-size Sprinter van and smaller Metris (aka V-class in the rest of the world) have long existed, they are commercial vehicles sent to finishing school to renounce their blue-collar roots and gain an appreciation for the finer things in life, such as sound deadening, multiple touchscreens, and kingly seats worthy of coddling royal bums—or at least maybe the Kardashians'. The VLE, on the other hand, is new from the ground up, a design dedicated to passenger comfort first and very little manual labor if it can help it.
You can fit up to eight passengers with rear bench seats, but it's the two/two/two configuration that really channels the private-jet-on-wheels vibe. There's not a bad seat in the house, but we did notice that the driver's seat in the more upscale Exclusive trim we tried has less fore-and-aft travel and backrest adjustment than the seats in the less swanky versions. Mercedes says it has to do with the hardware for the fancy electrically adjustable sliding rear seats (MB calls it a "seat ballet"), but it also, maybe not so inadvertently, reserves more room for the pampered passengers paying the fare.
Like a minivan, the VLE has dual power-sliding side doors with roll-down windows. Interior B-pillar-mounted switches allow you to operate either side with the flip of a tiny selector switch. Additionally, they can be operated by the driver or via remote access with an app. Tight curbside entry and exit in urban environments has never been so easy.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2028 Mercedes-Benz VLE-class EV for sale near 534236
We'd be remiss if we didn't point out the VLE's party trick: the 31.3-inch panoramic screen tucked up in the ceiling. Dubbed the MBUX Rear Space Experience, the screen teams with the available Burmester audio system with Dolby Atmos sound processing to create a mini theater experience sure to entertain even the most miserable cinema Pecksniff. The startup sequence, summoned by either of the wireless remotes, can even be programmed to raise the window sunshades as the screen deploys, for maximum dramatic effect. And in a nod to the proletariat, the screen is available even on the base model. 
Front- or All-Wheel Drive, Both Capable of Turning Around in Tight Spots
Without motors, the VLE is just a fancy shed with a home theater installed. Luckily, it offers a choice of two powertrains: the VLE300, which has a single 272-hp motor driving the front wheels, and the VLE400, with a dual-motor setup providing all-wheel drive and 413 horsepower. The vehicle features an 800-volt architecture, has a nickel-manganese-cobalt battery with 115 kWh of usable capacity, and can add a claimed 220 miles in just 15 minutes when connected to the appropriate 300-kW DC fast-charger.
For our first stint at the wheel, we grabbed a Europe-market VLE400 in Obsidian Black with AMG Line Plus trim. With a combined 413 horsepower from its dual motors and rolling on 21-inch AMG twin-spoke wheels, the VLE sets off in eerie silence, slow-rolling across a pebble pathway with unhurried grace. The air suspension offers a supple ride at low speeds, perfect for creeping around movie lots and under boutique-hotel entryway canopies. In the tight urban streets of Bilbao, Spain, the VLE's secret weapon reveals itself: seven degrees of rear-wheel steering.
Put simply, it renders similarly sized urban vehicles without rear-wheel steering almost pointless. The Euro models we drove measure 209.0 inches long, with a wheelbase just over 131.6 inches, granting the VLE a turning radius of just 35.7 feet; that's nearly six feet less than the Chevrolet Suburban's best curb-to-curb radius of 41.5 feet. Granted, at 226.3 inches long and with a wheelbase of 134.1 inches, the Suburban has more length to rotate, but given the VLE's vast interior and easier third-row access, it makes the 'Burban seem kind of oafish.
There is a car-service-sized asterisk, however, as the U.S. will only get the long-wheelbase VLE, which is nearly seven inches longer overall and has a wheelbase of 138.0 inches. Its turning circle is a bit larger at 37.5 feet.
It's with that same nimble attitude that the VLE slipped through tiny, congested streets, pivoting around human pylons crossing with little regard for the traffic circling about them. Ten external cameras, five radar sensors, and 12 ultrasonic sensors all work diligently to keep the VLE driver from unplanned introductions to the flesh, concrete, and steel obstacles in their path.
Automated helpers include a park-assistance function, which worked with about 80 percent success in our repeated tries at slipping the VLE into tight spots, and an available "Reverse Maneuvering Function." Basically, it remembers the last 490 feet of travel and can retrace that path in reverse. Weave your way through a tight parking situation only to find forward progress blocked? Push a few buttons, and the VLE expertly backs you out of the mess you just created. It's a bit unnerving at first, but it performed flawlessly.
Highway Stars and Efficiency Champs
Out of the urban jungle, highway travel is serene, as you might expect. There's plenty of power in the dual-motor version, conversation is easy in the hushed cabin, the seats are supportive, and the audio is rich. In contrast to the cushy low-speed ride, above 40 mph or so, pavement imperfections can sometimes echo through the chassis, the suspension taking a beat or two to settle after impact. It's but a small price to pay for the soft tuning that blunts the initial impact.
As for range, Mercedes claims up to 650 kilometers based on the wildly optimistic WLTP test procedure, which would translate to about 343 of our EPA miles. In a test of efficiency, Mercedes plotted a 20-mile loop through the tight streets of Bilbao and the hilly countryside surrounding it, posting a "best of" Mercedes-employee consumption average of 15.2 kWh per 100 kilometers, and presented a challenge to beat it.
Armed with a steady accelerator foot, the maximum regeneration setting, plenty of predictive traffic and terrain observation, switched-off climate control, closed windows, and a chatty co-driver, we humbly humbled the Mercedes staffers, beating them with a consumption rate of 14.8 kWh per 100 kilometers. This marks only the second time C/D has ever won an efficiency challenge and the first time without resorting to highly dubious rule exploitation (though we did briefly consider drafting another VLE with its tailgate locked in the open position).
On Sale in Europe Soon; Tomorrow, the World
The VLE's stateside arrival is targeted for the second half of 2027. Many details remain in flux. While Mercedes executives are confident that the commercial car-service market will command 80 percent of European sales, they're less sure about the U.S. mix between car service and personal use. Mercedes is uncharacteristically cavalier here, with one exec telling C/D he didn't know how the product mix would play out in the United States. But because the U.S. market responds quickly, Mercedes will "know how to proceed soon after launch, listening to customers' input to develop packages and features." Furthermore, he confided that expectations are "realistic," and planners don't think the VLE will sell 100,000 units out of the gate, although they "hope to catch a lot of customers from outside Mercedes-Benz."
Specific trims destined for our shores won't be determined until closer to launch, and even then, they may not share the same naming scheme as the Euro models. We're told that the U.S. will lean toward more luxurious variants. Manufaktur customization options are on the table, if customers "are willing to pay our price." Even a Maybach version is not out of the question.
Maybe the Mercedes folks are right, and "mini" is too diminutive for such a vehicle. But the shape is undeniably that of a van. "Limovan" has a nice ring to it.

title: 2026 Ford E-Transit Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Beth Nichols
text:
2026 Ford E-Transit
- Attractive pricing, available in two lengths and three roof heights, giant cargo hold.
- Can't tow, unavailable with rear seats, the gas Transit hauls more.
- The E-Transit is an affordable and eco-friendly cargo van, well suited for last-mile delivery services and tradespeople with lots to carry.

Overview
As its prefix implies, the E-Transit is the electric version of the Ford Transit full-size van. A 266-hp electric motor—instead of a V-6 engine—drives the rear wheels and draws its juice from a 89.0-kWh lithium-ion battery instead of a gas tank. Its 159-mile range is respectable for such a large vehicle, and the van is capable of DC fast-charging.
There's no passenger version, but the E-Transit does seat two and offers two different body lengths and three different roof heights. It's also reasonably priced, undercutting its electric rivals by thousands. The cabin isn't fancy by any means, but fleet drivers should find the controls easy to use (and clean), and shoppers can opt for features like blind-spot monitoring and a 360-degree camera system to make travel safer.
Expert Tip: Though it's more expensive, the electric Mercedes-Benz eSprinter offers better range, payload, and towing figures.
What's New for 2026?
This year, Ford has upgraded the E-Transit's onboard telematics system with better fleet management features. An 8.0-inch digital gauge display is also available. Buyers can also now opt for Ford's Co-Pilot360 2.0 suite of driver-assistance features, which includes adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Ford E-Transit to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
- EV Motor: 266-hp single motor
- Drivetrain: rear-wheel drive
The E-Transit uses a single electric motor that powers the rear wheels. Rated at 266 horsepower, the motor gives up a few ponies to the standard Transit's 275-hp gas-sipping V-6, but its 317 pound-feet of torque handily tops the gas engine's 262-lb-ft figure. Furthermore, full torque is on tap right at step-off, whereas the gas V-6 needs to spin its crank to 3750 rpm to make peak torque. Ford claims it revised the E-Transit's suspension system relative to that of the gasoline-powered Transit in a bid to improve the battery-powered van's handling. When we get a chance to test-drive the E-Transit, we'll report our driving impressions here.
0–60-MPH Times
We haven't had the chance to strap our test gear to an E-Transit yet. Once we do, we'll report our findings here.
Towing and Payload Capacity
- Max Towing: not recommended
- Max Payload: 3320-4201 pounds
Although Ford of Europe claims a max towing capacity of 4409 pounds for the overseas E-Transit, Ford's American arm does not recommend towing with the U.S.-spec E-Transit. Max payload ratings range between 3320 and 4201 pounds, depending on the configuration.
In Comparison: Benz's eSprinter can carry between 2624 and 3516 pounds, and it's able to tow up to 4277 pounds. Depending on whether you select the Delivery or Cargo variant, the Ram ProMaster EV boasts a maximum payload of 2030 or 3020 pounds, and like the Ford, it's not up for towing.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- Claimed EV Range: 159 miles
The E-Transit's 89.0-kWh lithium-ion battery affords up to 159 miles of driving range on a full charge, per Ford. The automaker offers a mobile kit for charging the E-Transit at home. It also sells a more powerful charging station for garage use. Ford claims a 180-kW DC fast-charger adds 67 miles of range in 15 minutes and that Level 2 charging takes as little as six hours to bring the battery from zero to 100 percent.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
Full-size vans are not subject to fuel-economy standards and therefore don't receive efficiency estimates. When we get the chance to test the E-Transit for ourselves, we'll subject it to our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test and update this page with results.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: Unlike the standard gasoline-powered Transit, which offers numerous interior configurations, the E-Transit packs seats for two, though opting to delete the passenger seat brings that total down to one. The E-Transit's spartan interior reflects its utilitarian agenda. Still, the van's relatively compliant suspension tune and carlike interior bits make it a better on-road companion than your typical work truck.
Cargo Capacity: Cargo capacity depends on body length and roof height. Buyers can pair the long body (the shortest available on the E-Transit) with a low, medium, or high roof for 312, 401, or 453 cubic feet of storage space, or they can opt for the extended-length, high-roof model, which boasts 536 cubes.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 12.0-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Audio Systems: 4-speaker stereo (standard), 6-speaker stereo (optional)
All E-Transit cargo vans come with a 12.0-inch infotainment system that runs Ford's Sync 4 operating system. An onboard 4G LTE modem provides a Wi-Fi hotspot, and a complimentary three-year subscription to Ford Pro E-Telematics provides vital vehicle data and tracking features for fleet managers. The van also includes a vehicle preconditioning feature that can set the climate and other functions while still connected to the charging station, saving vital battery charge and ensuring maximum driving range.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The E-Transit comes standard with basic driver-assistance features. Additional available features include adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and a 360-degree camera system.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, lane-keeping assist
- Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature, blind-spot monitoring, 360-degree camera system
For information about the E-Transit's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Ford's standard warranty package falls in line with the industry norm. The E-Transit offers an eight-year/100,000-mile warranty on its battery components, but Ford doesn't offer any complimentary scheduled maintenance.
- Limited Warranty: three years or 36,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: five years or 60,000 miles
- Battery-Component Warranty: eight years or 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

title: 2025 Mercedes-Benz EQS Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
2025 Mercedes-Benz EQS
- Plush cabin, impressive long-range capability, loaded with tech features.
- The overly digital dashboard won't find fans among luddites, brake pedal feel is weird, the jellybean shape isn't for everyone.
- The EV analogue of Mercedes's S-class flagship, the EQS sedan delivers on luxury but its driving experience disappoints and its looks are polarizing.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2025 Mercedes-Benz EQS for sale near 264200
367–390 Miles
5 Seats
Electric
All-Wheel Drive, Rear-Wheel Drive
4 Years/50,000 Miles
Overview
The Mercedes-Benz S-class has long been recognized as the brand's luxury flag-bearer, and the all-electric 2025 EQS offers an equally opulent experience—but in a body so softly rounded, it looks like it has been melting in the summer sun. Available with one motor and rear-wheel drive or two motors and all-wheel drive, the EQS can be optimized for an extended driving range or outfitted with up to 516 horsepower for maximum acceleration. Speaking of range, even the least efficient EQS580 model was able to travel for over 350 miles in our highway range test—no small accomplishment. Tech lovers will find plenty to like inside the EQS's cabin too, with a total of three screens embedded into the dashboard and all manner of connectivity and driver-assistance features incorporated into the architecture. Our chief complaints about the EQS are its blasé driving personality and its mushy, disconnected brake pedal feel. If you're prioritizing a plush, quiet ride the EQS delivers exactly that. That its rivals—a list that includes the BMW i7 and the Lucid Air—offer both similar panache and better road manners makes the EQS a harder sell. 
What's New for 2025?
The EQS receives a new front-end treatment for 2025 that replaces the faux grille and its inset logo with a three-bar motif and a standing hood ornament in an attempt to make the EV sedan look a little more like the gas-powered S-class. A more important upgrade lies beneath the EQS's floor, though: Mercedes has swapped last year's 108.4-kWh battery for a larger 118.0-kWh unit to boost range. Changes to the car's regenerative braking system will also contribute to a longer driving range estimate, according to the company. The cabin has been gussied up a bit, too, with more chrome accents and contrasting piping on the rear seat's pillows. The top-spec Pinnacle trim can now be had with an Executive Interior package that adds a reclining rear seat and a front-passenger seat that can fold toward the dashboard to create more rear-seat legroom.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2025 Mercedes-Benz EQS to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
The single motor on the rear axle of the EQS450+ produces 335 horsepower and 419 pound-feet of torque. The EQS450 4Matic adds an electric motor to the front axle for all-wheel drive. Combined horsepower holds at 335 horsepower, but torque climbs to 590 pound-feet. The EQS580 4Matic makes a combined 516 hp and 611 pound-feet of torque. Every EQS rides on an adaptive air suspension and wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches. Standard rear-axle steering can angle the rear wheels up to 10 degrees to tighten the turning circle. With the 207.3-inch-long EQS being just four inches shorter than a Chevy Tahoe, rear-wheel steering makes the sedan easier to maneuver in tight spots and increases stability at high speeds. In our testing, we found the luxury sedan delivered the kind of quiet and silken ride that one would expect of an electric Mercedes flagship. The improvements made to the braking system for 2025 make the brake-pedal feel more normal, and suspension upgrades help the car feel more balanced in corners.
0–60-MPH Times
In our testing, the 2025 EQS450 4Matic got to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds. The previous rear-wheel-drive EQS450+ accelerated to 60 mph in 5.4 seconds. The more powerful EQS580 hit 60 mph in just 3.7 seconds in our testing.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
All 2025 EQS models feature a lithium-ion battery pack with a usable capacity of 118.0 kWh, an increase in capacity over last year's model. The EPA rates the most efficient model, the EQS450+, to deliver a driving range of 390 miles per charge. The all-wheel-drive EQS450 4Matic is rated for 367 miles and the more powerful EQS580 is rated for 371 miles. With 200-kW fast-charging capability, every EQS can replenish its battery from 10 to 80 percent in 31 minutes. Plugged into a 240-volt Level 2 charger, getting from 10 to 100 percent takes 11.5 hours. On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test route, which is part of our extensive testing regimen, we observed an impressive 400 miles of range in the 2025 EQS450 4Matic model.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
The EPA estimates that the base EQS450+ will return 98 MPGe both in the city and on the highway. With the EQS450 4Matic’s use of an additional electric motor on the front axle, it takes a hit down to 91 MPGe city and 93 highway. Surprisingly, the highest-output EQS580 4Matic trim is more efficient than the EQS450 4Matic, with a combined rating of 93 MPGe—not bad for a 516-horsepower big-body luxury sedan. When we get the chance, we'll take the 2025 EQS on our 75-mph highway fuel economy route and update this story with its real-world fuel economy result. For more information about the EQS’s fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
It’s not like Mercedes would forget how to make an S-Class—or in this case, it's equivalent—just because the powertrain was switched from gas to electric. The interior furnishings satisfy every expectation and make a plush home for massive amounts of tech. Even the entry-level EQS450+ comes with LED headlights, air suspension, a panoramic roof, augmented video navigation that overlays arrows onto the map to identify lanes and turns, Burmester 3D audio, wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, cabin climate preconditioning, adaptive cruise control, active park assistant, 64-color ambient lighting, and much more. And there’s also the standard 56-inch-wide Hyperscreen, actually three screens-in-one that turn the entire instrument panel into a glass-panel display. There's epic spread-out room for NBA players in the cabin as well. Thanks to a completely flat floor and a lengthy 126.4-inch wheelbase, the EQS has a cavernous interior. Cargo space is also especially generous, thanks to its large hatchback.
Infotainment and Connectivity
The EQS features a fingerprint scanner that activates individual driver profiles, the "Hey Mercedes" voice-command system, and augmented-reality navigation in the head-up display. Every model also includes six USB-C ports throughout the cabin and Burmester audio. Mercedes’ MBUX infotainment software runs on the standard Hyperscreen. The display includes the 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, the 17.7-inch central touchscreen, and the 12.3-inch passenger-side touchscreen, all fronted by a door-to-door glass panel that makes it look like one huge screen. Planned over-the-air (OTA) updates for vehicles with the Entertainment Package Plus will add features like the YouTube web app and Dolby Atmos surround sound.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The 2025 EQS comes packed with standard driver-assistance technology, including adaptive cruise control and self-parking assist. For more information about the EQS's crash test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Standard lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist
- Standard adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes' limited and powertrain warranties are competitive with other German automakers, but its terms aren't particularly noteworthy. There's also no complimentary maintenance, which is something BMW offers.
- Limited warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Electrical components are covered for 10 years or 155,000 miles
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance

title: 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Beth Nichols
text:
2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS
- Admirable electric range, opulent interior, impressive tech suite.
- Not the handsomest of Benzes, not our favorite brake-pedal feel, rivals are quicker.
- The electric EQS may have the cabin of an S-class, but it lacks the flagship's elegance.

All-Wheel Drive, Rear-Wheel Drive

Overview
The electric EQS liftback sedan is every bit as swanky and serene inside as its gas-powered equivalent, the Mercedes-Benz S-class. Its glass-topped, three-screen dashboard gives the cabin a futuristic feel, but there's still plenty of old-school luxury here, with yards of stitched leather and smatterings of wood or carbon-fiber trim throughout.
Customers have a trio of models to choose from, all of which offer at least 360 miles of range and 335 ponies. But while the lineup-topping 519-hp EQS580 4Matic is quicker than even the V-8-powered S580, it's still behind the EV pace with a 3.7-second dash to 60. Moreover, the EQS just doesn't have the same aesthetic or dynamic panache as the gas-powered S-class, but then again, what does?
Expert Tip: The Lucid Air and Porsche Taycan post much more impressive numbers than the EQS.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#13 in Best Luxury Electric CarsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
Every EQS buyer now receives a NACS adapter, so they can charge at Tesla Supercharger stations. Benz lowered pricing too, which is always nice to see.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
- EV Motors: 335-hp single motor, 335-hp dual motors, 516-hp dual motors
- Drivetrains: rear-wheel drive, all-wheel drive
The base EQS makes 335 horsepower and 419 pound-feet of torque from a single motor that drives the rear wheels. The EQS450 4Matic adds an electric motor to the front axle for all-wheel drive. This has no effect on the EV's horsepower rating, but it does increase the model's torque to 590 pound-feet. At the top of the lineup sits the dual-motor EQS580 4Matic, which produces a combined 516 horses and 611 pound-feet.
The EQS isn't small—its length is within four inches of a Chevy Tahoe—but it boasts rear-axle steering, which makes it easy to maneuver in tight spots. The system also helps increase stability at high speeds.
With its standard air suspension, this luxury sedan delivers the kind of quiet and silken ride that one would expect of an electric Mercedes flagship. The improvements made to the braking system for 2025 make the brake-pedal feel more normal, and suspension upgrades help the car feel more balanced in corners.
0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Tests: 5.4 seconds (EQS450+), 4.7 seconds (EQS450 4Matic), 3.7 seconds (EQS580 4Matic)
In Comparison: Among performance EVs, the EQS isn't very impressive. The base, rear-drive Porsche Taycan, for instance, hits 60 in 4.1 seconds, and the 536-hp Taycan 4S gets there in 3.1.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- C/D Range Tests: 400 miles (EQS450 4Matic)
- EPA EV Range: 367–390 miles
A 118.0-kWh lithium-ion battery provides the juice for every EQS model. The EPA says the base car can go 390 miles per charge, which is pretty good for a full-size electric sedan. The 4Matic models aren't going as far; the EQS450's estimated range is actually lower than the EQS580's at 367 miles versus 371.
On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test route, which is part of our extensive testing regimen, we observed an impressive 400 miles of range in the 2025 EQS450 4Matic model.
A half-hour on a DC fast-charger (running at 200 kilowatts) is enough to restore this EV's battery charge from 10 to 80 percent. With the EQS plugged into a 240-volt Level 2 station, it takes about 11.5 hours to top it off.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
- EPA City Ratings: 91-98 MPGe
- EPA Highway Ratings: 93-98 MPGe
The 2026 EQS450+ earns 98-MPGe estimates across the board. (MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV fuel efficiency.) Dual-motor models take a fuel-economy hit, with the EQS450 4Matic seeing 91 MPGe city and 93 highway, and the EQS580 4Matic trim returning 93 MPGe in both cycles.
We'll update this page with real-world results when we have the opportunity to test the updated models. For more information about the EQS's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: The electric S-class analogue is as opulent and roomy inside as you'd expect. The amenities are endless, and the heated and ventilated leather seats are plush. Shoppers can option a heated steering wheel, laminated sound-deadening glass, active ambient lighting, and a cabin-fragrance system for some extra dough.
Second Row: So long as they slouch in their seats, NBA players could sprawl out in the EQS's second row, which is available with heating, ventilation, and massage functions.
Cargo Capacity: The EQS can hold a surprising amount of stuff in the back, thanks in part to its fold-flat rear seats. The yawning liftgate makes loading easy, too. In our testing, we fit eight carry-on suitcases in the EQS's trunk. With the rear seats folded, we fit 23.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 17.7-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio System: 15-speaker Burmester stereo
The brand's dash-spanning Hyperscreen is a cool-looking piece of tech, situating three displays—a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, a 17.7-inch central touchscreen, and a 12.3-inch passenger panel—beneath one sheet of glass.
The infotainment system responds to voice prompts, finger taps, and steering-wheel controls and allows occupants to stream video from apps like YouTube and Disney+ when the car is stationary. Benz also offers two head-up displays, with the more costly option featuring augmented-reality overlays.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The 2026 EQS comes loaded with many driver-assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, a surround-view camera system, advanced parking tech, and more.
- Standard Safety Features: adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, blind-spot monitoring
For information about the EQS's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes-Benz's limited and powertrain warranties are on par with what other luxury automakers offer. BMW one-ups M-B by providing some complimentary service visits for its EV buyers.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Battery-Component Warranty: 10 years or 155,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

- Impressive driving range estimates, agile and nimble feel in corners, comfortable ride.
- Array of screens inside can be overwhelming, small rear seat, some cheap interior materials.
- The new electric version of the CLA is pleasant to drive and promises more range than its rivals, making it an attractive option among EV sedans.

Overview
The CLA-class has been the entry point to the Mercedes-Benz lineup for years, and as the fastback sedan enters its third generation, it's spawning an electric variant. While a gas-powered CLA will still live on, the electric CLA is offered either as the CLA250+ or the CLA350. The CLA250+ comes with a single-motor rear-wheel drive setup, while the dual-motor CLA350 offers all-wheel drive and more power. Driving range is the CLA EV's most impressive metric, though; the EPA estimates the CLA's driving range at up to 374 miles per charge. Mercedes is promising impressively quick DC fast-charging capability, too. The CLA will challenge established EV sedans such as the BMW i4 and the Tesla Model 3.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#3 in Best Electric Sedans and HatchbacksCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class EV with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
The next-gen CLA-class launches for the 2026 model year, and the lineup includes an EV for the very first time. Mercedes-Benz has developed an entirely new platform for the forthcoming CLA, which will also provide the basis for a pair of small SUVs as well as a station-wagon variant of the CLA-class sedan.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class EV to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
The CLA250+ will be the base model of the EV range, packing a 268-hp electric motor powering the rear wheels. A two-speed transmission is standard, rather than the one-speed found in most EVs. Also found on the Porsche Taycan, a two-speed transmission aims to improve highway efficiency and performance. The CLA350 adds a front-mounted motor, granting all-wheel drive and boosting output to 349 horsepower. When we drove the CLA EV in Europe, we found it to offer smooth power and a comfortable ride. The CLA250+ is responsive enough when merging or passing, but the CLA350 is the one to buy if you desire quick acceleration. However, we preferred the 250+ model's lighter steering and suspension tune, as the 350 feels heavier and less nimble in corners.
0–60-MPH Times
Mercedes-Benz estimates that the rear-wheel-drive CLA250+ will hit 60 mph in 6.6 seconds while the more powerful all-wheel-drive CLA350 can do it in just 4.8 seconds. We'll test these claims for ourselves once we get a chance to evaluate the CLA EVs at our test track.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
The CLA EV is the first car in the Mercedes-Benz lineup to ride on the company's new 800-volt architecture. It comes with an 85.0-kWh battery pack, and the EPA estimates that the CLA250+ can travel up to 374 miles before needing a charge. The CLA350 4Matic model is rated for 312 miles per charge. Mercedes claims that the CLA can charge at up to 320 kilowatts on an adequately powerful DC fast-charger; by our estimates, this means it can add around 150 miles of range in just 10 minutes. The CLA will be equipped with a NACS port and will be able to charge at Tesla Superchargers, although, because those stations use 400-volt systems, Mercedes says you'll need a converter to do so.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
The EPA estimates that the CLA EV will deliver up to 127 MPGe in the city and 124 MPGe on the highway. MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV fuel efficiency. For more information about the CLA-class EV's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
The CLA EV's cabin has space for four, an all-glass roof, and futuristic styling elements. Although it's a small car, the CLA's interior feels open and spacious, with a flat floor in the back seat and an open-concept cockpit design with decent storage options. Legroom in the back is still tight, though. We expect the Superscreen—a new, dashboard-spanning combination of three large upright displays—to be popular, even though it's not our cup of tea. All models come with heated and power-adjustable front seats, automatic climate control, four fast-charging USB-C ports, and the aforementioned fixed glass roof. Opt for the AMG Line package, and you'll get some sporty flair with a flat-bottomed steering wheel, red contrasting stitching for the upholstery, and brushed stainless steel pedals.
Infotainment and Connectivity
Digital screens comprise most of the CLA EV's dashboard. A 10.3-inch gauge cluster and a 14.0-inch central touchscreen are standard, while a second 14.0-inch passenger display is optional. When equipped with all three, Mercedes-Benz calls it Superscreen. We call it superfluous, but we're curious to try it out to see if it's as overwhelming as it sounds. A 16-speaker Burmester stereo is also available as an option, and it features Dolby Atmos technology for spatial audio.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Driver-assistance features, such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automated emergency braking, are all standard on the CLA EV. For more information about the CLA-class EV's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features are likely to include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection
- Standard lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Available adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes provides limited and powertrain coverages for its current production models that align with most rival luxury automakers. However, unlike BMW and Jaguar, the company doesn't provide any complimentary maintenance.
- Limited warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Electrical components are covered for eight years or 100,000
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance

author: Frankie Cruz
text:
2024 Mercedes-Benz eSprinter
- Decent driving range, spacious cargo area, more agile than expected for its size.
- Accelerating to cruising speeds requires patience, limited to just one size, no passenger-hauling version offered.
- The eSprinter is another option for fleet owners and tradesmen who want to deliver packages or shuttle cargo in a quiet, eco-friendly way.
For Sale Near You

2 Seats

Overview
The Mercedes-Benz eSprinter electric van electrifies the brand's workhorse cargo hauler. While it's been selling small electric vans in Europe for some time, the eSprinter joins the US market in 2024. It'll take a keen eye to tell the eSprinter from the gas-powered Sprinter van. Underneath, however, Mercedes has designed an all-new architecture that's home to a 113.0-kWh battery pack located in the eSprinter's belly and an electric motor driving the rear wheels. While the EPA hasn't weighed in with a driving range estimate yet, we expect it to be around 230 miles per charge. That's not as much as Mercedes's other EVs—the list of which includes the EQE and EQS sedans—but it will still be more than enough for delivery companies and tradesmen who often stick to local territory.
What's New for 2024?
The Mercedes-Benz eSprinter is all-new for the 2024 model year but wears a nearly identical outfit to the gas-powered Sprinter.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
The base eSprinter comes with a rear-wheel drive electric powertrain that makes 134 horsepower but a more powerful 201-hp version is also available. A 113.0-kWh battery pack is located in the eSprinter's underside between the front and rear axles. The eSprinter is limited to a top speed of 75 miles per hour regardless of which power output you choose. Getting up to that speed takes a little patience, and we imagine a rear end full of mail parcels or plumbing supplies will only exacerbate the eSprinter's pokiness. Handling is more controlled than expected for a vehicle this size. In our experience, the eSprinter's ride was well-damped and body roll was nicely curbed.
0–60-MPH Times
After driving the eSprinter, we estimate it will take 12.7 seconds to hit 60 mph with the more powerful motor; going with the entry-level 134-hp version will likely add several seconds to that number.
Towing and Payload Capacity
The eSprinter offers 488 cubic feet of cargo space, a bit shy of the gas Sprinter's 533-cu-ft cargo capacity. The maximum payload capacity for the eSprinter is 2,624 pounds, which is less than half that of the gas-powered Sprinter, but still amounts to a whole lot of cargo. Likewise, the eSprinter's 4200-pound towing capacity is lower than it is in the gas-powered Sprinter.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
The official EPA range estimate has not yet been released, but we expect to see it come in at around 230 miles per charge. Mercedes says the battery can be charged from 10 percent to 80 percent in 42 minutes using a DC fast charger. The total charge time for a completely depleted battery will be over 12 hours using a conventional 240-volt outlet.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
The EPA doesn't issue fuel economy ratings for commercial vehicles such as the eSprinter. When we get a chance to test it for ourselves, we'll take the van on or 75-mph highway fuel economy route to determine its real-world fuel economy. 
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
The eSprinter is offered only as a long-wheelbase van with a high roofline and features 488 cubic feet of cargo space, which is fairly close to what the regular Sprinter offers (533 cubic feet). Since it's a Mercedes, you can expect slightly more interior refinement than its main competitor, the Ford E-Transit, but don't expect S- or even C-class levels of luxury here. Options for making delivery life more palatable include heated and pivoting front seats, a heated windshield, electric folding exterior mirrors, air-conditioning, an electric sliding door and step, a digital rearview mirror, and more.
Infotainment and Connectivity
The eSprinter features the latest generation of Mercedes-Benz's infotainment software, which includes a voice control assistant. In addition to voice control, the system can also be operated via a touchscreen, touchpad, and touch-sensitive steering-wheel-mounted buttons. A larger 10.3-inch touchscreen display is optional, and cloud-based services to support fleet owners are too.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Mercedes provides the eSprinter with a list of standard driver-assistance technology, including blind-spot monitoring, crosswind assist, and automated emergency braking. It also warns the driver if it detects signs of drowsiness or inattention. For more information about the Sprinter's crash test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes-Benz's limited warranty on the eSprinter is typical for this class. However, its powertrain coverage is longer than most. Mercedes also doesn't pay for any scheduled maintenance.

- Lacks cargo space behind the third row, many desirable features cost extra, high price.
- The GLS-class is large, fast, and comfortable, but its strong suit is its delightful driving character.

Overview
The GL-class is dead, long live the GLS-class! Mercedes-Benz’s renamed three-row SUV family is as big and bad as ever, now with updated powertrains and a lightly revised exterior. This family hauler seats seven adults and can swallow up to 94 cubic feet of cargo. The stately exterior and luxe interior do justice to the Mercedes-Benz name, and prodigious acceleration will strike fear into the hearts of lesser automobiles. Competition is stiff, but the GLS-class more than holds its own, which is why it earned a place among our 10Best Trucks and SUVs.
What's New for 2017?
Mercedes renamed the GL-class as the GLS-class for 2017 to better parallel the nomenclature of its sedan lineup. All GLS models now use an automatic stop/start system, which helps conserve fuel in city driving. Inside, Benz’s updated COMAND system has a touchpad in addition to the existing rotary knob. Other revisions include new ambient lighting and trim colors, a three-spoke steering wheel, and an available nappa leather interior.

Engine, Transmission, and Performance
GLS-class buyers are confronted with a choice between three powerful, competent powertrains, all of which provide ample motivation for this Benz brawler. The GLS350d comes with a 3.0-liter turbodiesel engine that produces 255 horsepower and a prodigious 455 pound-feet of torque. The powerplant found in the GLS450 is a purring and muscular 362-hp twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6. And a stout 449-hp twin-turbo 4.7-liter V-8 powers the GLS550. All engines mate with a nine-speed automatic transmission and an all-wheel drive system. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 is the real star of the lineup—in our testing, it was as quick as the competition’s V-8s. The GLS-class is a big machine, but thanks to above-average driving dynamics, it never feels clumsy. Although it sometimes betrays its size—long braking stops and a soft suspension are the main culprits—the big Merc is respectably adept on the road. Thanks in part to its standard air suspension, the GLS-class rides like the luxury cruiser it is.
Fuel Economy
EPA fuel-economy testing and reporting procedures have changed over time. For the latest numbers on current and older vehicles, visit the EPA’s website and select Find & Compare Cars.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
While the GLS-class hasn’t yet achieved the level of opulence of the Mercedes-Benz S-class, it’s an appropriately cushy cockpit for one of the brand’s best SUVs. Certain interior features that should be standard at this price point are extra-cost options, such as leather seats, a power-adjustable front-passenger’s seat, ventilated seats, and three-zone climate control. Easy cargo loading and a wealth of space in an elegant package make the GLS-class an excellent choice for those who want to transport their stuff in style. The GLS’s cargo area is cavernous behind the first row of seats, respectable behind the second row, but cramped aft of the third row.
Infotainment and Connectivity
The GLS-class can be outfitted with the latest version of the Mercedes COMAND infotainment system. It’s mostly a successful application, though the touchpad can impede access to the rotary dial. The standard infotainment system is bare bones compared with the setups in other luxury vehicles. It has an 8.0-inch screen, two USB ports, eight-speaker audio, and Bluetooth connectivity. Access to SiriusXM satellite radio, navigation, Apple CarPlay, voice commands, and the new touchpad are all limited to the upgraded infotainment system, which is standard in the GLS550 but only available as part of a Premium package in the other trims.

title: 2019 Mercedes GLS-class Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Eric Stafford
text:
2019 Mercedes-Benz GLS-class
Car and Driver
Accolades- Above-average driving dynamics, stellar powertrains, spacious and luxurious.
- High price, expected features cost extra, lacks cargo space behind the third row.
- Big and fast but composed and graceful, the GLS-class is a status symbol worthy of its place atop the SUV mountain.

Overview
            Hulking three-row SUVs are a product of America, a huge shiny mirror that reflects all of our excesses and immodesties. Several classic big utes—the Cadillac Escalade and the Lincoln Navigator among them—are, fittingly, produced by Detroit carmakers. But foreign companies have been studying the art of the luxury hauler, and the Mercedes-Benz GLS-class proves that those efforts are paying off. The 2019 Mercedes-Benz GLS-class is a stylish, spacious, and dynamically sound take on a family SUV. It may not have as much cargo space as a GMC Yukon XL, but there's no denying the touch of glamour that a three-pointed star brings to a vehicle. The GLS-class feels much smaller than its size on the road; it's surprisingly quick and nimble, and, unlike many others in the class, it isn't onerous to park. Those are the qualities that helped the GLS claim another 10Best Trucks and SUVs award, and since it's virtually unchanged for 2019, it remains at the top of the class. An all-new GLS-class will hit the market before the end of the year as a 2020 model.        
What's New for 2019?
The 2019 GLS-class receives a new limited-production Grand Edition model. Its interior upgrades include ambient lighting, leather dashboard, special wood trim, and premium Porcelain/Expresso Brown leather upholstery with stitched surfaces. The exterior adds unique badging, adaptive LED headlights, and either standard 20-inch wheels (GLS450) or 21-inchers (GLS550).
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2019 Mercedes-Benz GLS-class to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, Performance, and Towing
  Likes: Standard all-wheel drive, two powerful and competent powertrains, engaging driving dynamics.          
 Dislikes: Tows less than main rivals.          
The base engine found in the GLS450 is a purring and muscular 362-hp twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6, while a stout 449-hp twin-turbo 4.7-liter V-8 powers the GLS550. Both engines pair with standard all-wheel drive and a nine-speed automatic transmission, which is optimized for highway cruising. The nine-speed shifts smoothly and rarely stumbles, but the twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 is the real star—in our testing, it was as quick as the competition's V-8s. While the GLS can tow up to 7500 pounds, that's less than rivals such as the Escalade that can handle up to 8500 pounds.
Thanks in part to its standard air suspension, the GLS-class rides like the luxury cruiser it is. Bumps and pavement imperfections melt away in the standard Comfort setting; the available adaptive shocks stiffen the pillowy ride when Sport mode is selected. The GLS isn't designed for hard cornering, so drivers will notice body roll when pushing it hard, but for everyday driving, it delivers the coddling ride we expect from a Mercedes. Steering is accurate and keeps this big ute tracking straight on the highway, but there's almost no feedback from the road, and reaction to inputs is somewhat lazy. Stopping the GLS-class in its tracks is no mean feat, given that it tips the scales at more than 5300 pounds. When you first apply the pedal, there is sponginess to the feel of the pedal, but push through that and it feels firm and reassuring.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
With its hulking size and a pair of large-displacement engines, the GLS-class can guzzle gas with the best of them, but the V-6 model at least manages better mileage than several V-8–only competitors. The optional V-8 aligns more closely with the competition from General Motors and Nissan. We don't have test results for the GLS550, which is EPA-rated at 19 mpg highway, but we did test the GLS450, which matched its 22-mpg highway rating in our highway fuel-economy testing.
Interior, Infotainment, and Cargo
  Likes: Cushy cockpit, myriad luxury options, more third-row legroom than main rivals.             
 Dislikes: Not quite as flashy as an S-class, desirable features cost extra, limited luggage capacity behind third row.             
Certain interior features that should be standard at this price point are extra-cost options, such as leather seats, a power-adjustable front-passenger's seat, ventilated seats, and three-zone climate control. Others, including heated and cooled front cupholders, are welcome extras that add innovative touches to the cabin. The first- and second-row seats are very comfortable, and even the third row is roomy enough for adults. Power-folding second-row seats are optional and make access to the third row easy.
Don't let the 12-button number pad fool you: The GLS-class can be outfitted with the latest version of Mercedes' COMAND infotainment system. It's mostly a successful application, although the touchpad can impede access to the rotary dial. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are available but cost extra. All Mercedes owners have remote access to their vehicles via a smartphone app, which can remotely start a paired vehicle and either begin heating or cooling the cabin.
Easy cargo loading and a wealth of space in an elegant package make the GLS-class an excellent choice for those who want to transport their cargo in style. However, if maximum storage capacity in a luxury cruiser is a high priority for you, there are other SUVs that can carry even more. Depending on which seats are deployed, the GLS's cargo area is either cavernous or cramped. With all three rows in use, we could only squeeze three carry-on bags into the luggage compartment. With the second and third rows folded, we stuffed 34 carry-ons behind the front seats.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The GLS-class has not been fully crash-tested by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) or the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). Mercedes-Benz's outstanding driver-assistance technology is available on all models, but most features are optional extras. Even blind-spot monitoring, which is finding its way into much more affordable vehicles as a standard feature, is optional in the base GLS. Key safety features include:
- Available forward-collision warning and automated emergency braking
- Available lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist
- Available self-parking assist
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes-Benz's warranty package is average among luxury brands in coverage length, and it fails to offer the complimentary scheduled maintenance that some competitors have.
- Limited warranty covers 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers 4 years or 50,000 miles
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance

title: 2021 Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
2021 Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class
- High-tech connectivity features, roomy interior, smooth-running engines.
- Annoying infotainment touchpad, somewhat bland design, high-priced option packages.
- As a luxury three-row SUV, the GLS-class delivers, and its surprisingly athletic chassis makes it all the more appealing.

Overview
As the S-class of Benz's SUVs, the 2021 Mercedes GLS-class aims to deliver an undeniably upscale experience, and it succeeds. This large three-row SUV has room for the whole family and pampers everyone with its tech-rich cabin, comfortable ride, and fancy interior materials. Buyers can choose from either a 362-hp turbocharged inline-six or a 483-hp twin-turbo V-8, both of which benefit from a hybrid-assistance system. Despite that technology, neither powertrain provides very impressive fuel efficiency, but at least the GLS's EPA ratings are in line with those of rival SUVs such as the Land Rover Range Rover and the Lincoln Navigator. All-wheel drive comes standard, as does an air suspension, but Mercedes offers a pothole-sensing upgrade that also increases ground clearance.

What's New for 2021?
The GLS-class was new last year, so 2021 models see only a few changes. Four-zone automatic climate control, ventilated seats, and 20-inch aluminum wheels are newly standard. As is a parking-damage detection feature, which can alert an owner's smartphone via the Mercedes Me Connect app if the car senses a collision while parked.

Pricing and Which One to Buy
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
Two models are offered—the six-cylinder GLS450 and the eight-cylinder GLS580—and both feature some hybridization. The GLS450's turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six is silky smooth and good for 362 horsepower. The GLS580 is far more powerful, making 483 horsepower from its twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8. Despite its size, the GLS-class is easy to hustle on a twisty road, but it's not overly sporty or harsh over bumps. All models come standard with an air suspension, but Mercedes offers a trick new system called E-Active Body Control. It utilizes a forward-facing camera to scan for bumps and adjusts the suspension accordingly so riders won't feel those road imperfections. It's a cool technology but expensive, and we think most buyers will find the standard setup does a fine job.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
The EPA fuel-economy estimates for the GLS-class aren't great. The GLS450 earns 19 mpg in the city, 23 mpg on the highway, and 21 mpg combined. The GLS580 does worse, with 16 mpg, 21 mpg, and 18 mpg, respectively. In our real-world testing, the GLS450 performs a little better than its rating, managing 24 mpg on our 200-mile highway loop. The GLS580 returned a dismal 18 mpg in the same test. If fuel economy is a priority for you, the BMW X7 will be a better choice in the luxury-SUV department. A six-cylinder X7 xDrive40i managed an impressive 28 mpg in our highway test while an eight-cylinder xDrive50i delivered 24 mpg.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
Borrowing its dashboard and cockpit layout from the similarly new GLE-class SUV, this generation of GLS is far more modern than the one it replaces. It'll fit up to seven passengers but can be spec'd for six with the optional captain's chairs. Passenger space is generous in the first and second rows, and the third row, while not as spacious as the second, can accommodate an adult without too much complaining—something that can't be said of the wayback in the X7.
Infotainment and Connectivity
Two huge 12.3-inch digital displays take up the majority of the dashboard: One serves as a reconfigurable gauge display for the driver while the other handles infotainment duties and runs Mercedes-Benz's new MBUX software, which features an iPhone-like virtual assistant. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capability, in-dash navigation, and an on-board Wi-Fi hotspot are all standard. All GLS models come with a 13-speaker Burmester Surround Sound stereo, but if that's not enough for you, there's an available Burmester 3D audio system with an insane 26-speaker arrangement.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Neither the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) nor the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) have released crash-test results for the 2021 GLS-class. Mercedes-Benz offers several different types of driver-assistance features on this SUV, but the most interesting bits—such as a semi-autonomous driving mode—cost extra. Key safety features include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Available lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Available adaptive cruise control with a semi-autonomous driving mode
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Buyers of the GLS-class receive a four-year/50,000-mile warranty as standard, which is far from the best in this class. The Cadillac Escalade offers two more years of powertrain coverage, and the Lincoln Navigator comes with four years of complimentary scheduled maintenance if you go for the luxurious Black Label model.

While we have yet to take a recent GLS-class on our 75-mph fuel-economy route, the pre-update 2020 GLS450 performed a little better than its 23-mpg rating, delivering a 24-mpg result. For more information about the GLS's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
In Comparison: If fuel economy is a priority for you, the BMW X7 will be a better choice in the luxury SUV department. A six-cylinder X7 xDrive40i managed an impressive 28 mpg in our highway test.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: Borrowing its dashboard and cockpit layout from the GLE-class SUV, this generation of GLS is far more modern than the one it replaces. Fit and finish is great, and the standard combination of leatherette upholstery and brushed-aluminum trim looks suitably upscale, though many buyers will be tempted by Benz's sumptuous leather and wood options.
Second Row: The GLS will fit up to seven passengers but can be spec'd for six with the optional second-row captain's chairs. Passenger space is generous in the first and second rows.
Third Row: The third row, while not as spacious as the second, can accommodate an adult without too much complaining—something that can't be said of the wayback in the X7.
Cargo Capacity: Depending on how many seats you keep up in back, the GLS offers between 17 and 85 cubic feet of cargo room. Those numbers are on the low side for a vehicle in this class. IN our testing, we fit four carry-on suitcases behind the GLS's third row. With the third row down, we fit 16 suitcases, and with the second and third rows folded, we fit a total of 30.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 12.3-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio Systems: 13-speaker Burmester stereo (standard), 26-speaker Burmester stereo (optional)
Two huge 12.3-inch digital displays take up the majority of the GLS's dashboard. One serves as a reconfigurable gauge display for the driver, while the other handles infotainment duties and runs Mercedes-Benz's MBUX software, which features a Siri-like virtual assistant. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capability, built-in navigation, and an onboard Wi-Fi hotspot are standard. All GLS models come with a 13-speaker Burmester stereo, but if that's not enough for you, Benz offers another Burmester setup with twice as many speakers.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The GLS comes with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance features, but it has yet to receive the brand’s hands-free driving tech.
- Standard Safety Features: blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist
For information about the GLS's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
The GLS's warranty and maintenance terms are far from the best in this class. The Cadillac Escalade offers two more years of powertrain coverage, and the Lincoln Navigator comes with four years of complimentary scheduled maintenance if you go for the luxurious Black Label model.

title: 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Hybrid Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
- Home
- Mercedes-Benz
- GLE-Class Hybrid
2026 Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Hybrid
- Quiet interior when cruising, good electric-only driving range, nicely balanced ride and handling.
- Not as quick as key rivals, no third-row seat option, regenerative braking system doesn’t reclaim much energy.
- The GLE450e nails its luxury mission and adds a generous electric driving range to the equation for good measure.

Overview
As plug-in hybrid SUVs go, the 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLE450e is a good choice, offering an EPA-estimated 50 miles of range per charge with very little effect on its luxury package. It packs as many premium features and upscale ambiance inside as its nonhybrid counterpart, the GLE450.
The hybrid powertrain includes a turbocharged four-cylinder and an electric motor that combine for 381 horsepower. The GLE's chief rival, the BMW X5 xDrive50e, is quicker, but the X5’s electric range isn't as long, at only 40 miles vs. 50 for the Mercedes.
Expert Tip: The GLE-class hybrid is offered with only two rows of seats, so if you need a plug-in hybrid luxury SUV with a third row, you'll need to consider a rival such as the Lexus TX550h+ or the Volvo XC90 T8.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#5 in Best Hybrid Mid-Size Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Hybrid with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
Mercedes-Benz has made no significant changes to the GLE-class hybrid for 2026.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Hybrid to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
- Hybrid Powertrain: Turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder and one electric motor, 381 hp combined
- Transmission: 9-speed automatic
- Drivetrain: all-wheel-drive
The GLE450e's plug-in-hybrid powertrain comprises a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder and an electric motor that combine for a total of 381 horsepower. That makes it slightly more powerful than the 362-hp nonhybrid GLE450, but the 603-hp AMG-tuned GLE63 still rules the GLE-class lineup. The GLE450e feels spry around town, though, thanks to the electric motor's instant torque delivery. The nine-speed automatic transmission shuffles gears seamlessly, helping keep the GLE450e comfortable on long cruises.
Handling is more agile than expected for an SUV of this size, and the ride is comfortable—so long as you skip the optional upsized 21-inch wheels. The only part of the experience that lacks refinement is the regenerative braking system. In our testing, the GLE450e required a lengthy 176 feet to stop from 70 mph, and when using the maximum regeneration setting during normal driving, we failed to reclaim much energy.
Off-roading in the GLE450e is aided by the optional air-spring suspension system, which can be used to raise the SUV for more ground clearance and better approach and departure angles. All-wheel drive is standard across the lineup, as are an off-road driving mode and a hill-descent control system.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Test: 5.3 seconds
In Comparison: At our test track, the GLE450e hit 60 mph in 5.3 seconds. That's quick by class standards, but the X5 xDrive50e outran the Benz with a 3.9-second time.
Towing and Payload Capacity
- Max Towing: 7700 pounds
When equipped with an optional trailer hitch, the GLE450e can tow up to 7700 pounds.
In Comparison: The Porsche Cayenne E-Hybrid can tow slightly more at a maximum of 7716 pounds, but the X5 xDrive50e is only rated for up to 6603 pounds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- C/D Range Test: 53 miles
The GLE450e model comes with a 23.3-kWh battery pack, and it's rated to deliver 50 miles of range on a full charge. In our 75-mph real-world highway test, it beat that estimate with a 53-mile result. The X5 xDrive50e managed 33 miles of electric driving in the same test, while the Cayenne E-Hybrid Coupe we tested went 40 miles before depleting its battery.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
- C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 25 mpg
- EPA City Rating: 21 mpg
- EPA Highway Rating: 26 mpg
The GLE450e hybrid is rated at 21 mpg city and 26 mpg highway. In our highway fuel economy testing, it achieved 25 mpg. For more information about the GLE-class's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: The GLE450e's cabin delivers much the same luxury experience as the rest of the GLE lineup, with premium materials on every surface and plenty of comfort and convenience features. All models come with heated front seats with power adjustments and memory settings. Dual-zone automatic climate control, a power sunroof, ambient interior lighting, and a hands-free power liftgate are all included, too. There are plenty of upholstery color options, rendered in either faux or genuine leather hides.
Second Row: While the nonhybrid GLE models can be had with an optional third row of seats, the GLE450e is strictly a two-row affair, presumably to help make room for the hybrid system's battery pack.
Cargo Capacity: There's a 31.5-cubic-foot cargo hold behind the GLE450e's rear seat. In our testing, that proved to be enough space to hold 10 carry-on suitcases. When we folded the rear seat flat, we fit a total of 19.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 12.3-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Audio System: 8-speaker stereo (standard), 13-speaker Burmester stereo (optional)
Dual 12.3-inch infotainment displays stretch nearly the whole width of the dashboard and offer several ways to interact with the system, including the MBUX voice recognition system. Like Apple's Siri or Google's virtual assistant, MBUX can respond to many commands, thus enabling the driver to keep their hands on the wheel but still turn up the heat, switch on the ventilated seats, or tune to a specific radio station.
A touchpad on the center console allows for tactile interaction with the infotainment system, and the screen is also touch-sensitive. Still, the menus aren't all logically structured. Navigating them is better done when the GLE is parked. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, as well as a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot are all standard, which makes it a little easier to keep up with calls, texts, and other communication while on the move.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The GLE's standard suite of driver-assistance features includes only the basics; Mercedes makes you pay extra for desirable tech such as adaptive cruise control and lane-keeping assist.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, front and rear parking sensors
- Optional Safety Features: lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control
For information about the GLE-class's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Whereas BMW and Volvo include three years of maintenance in the price of any new X5 or XC90, Mercedes offers zero complimentary maintenance. As far as warranty policies go, the GLE's standard offerings are among the most basic in the luxury-car marketplace.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Electric Component Warranty: eight years or 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

title: 2018 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class Review, Pricing, and Specs
text:
2018 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class
- Distinctive styling, enthusiastic handling, long list of standard and available tech features.
- Cargo space lags behind rivals, tight back seat, stiff ride.
- The 2018 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class may not offer the luxury and interior room of some rivals, but it is fun to drive.

Overview
The Mercedes-Benz GLA-class has a higher ride height than its sedan counterpart—the CLA-class—which technically earns it crossover status, but only just. Its performance-oriented driving characteristics remind us more of a hot hatchback than an SUV, and enthusiast drivers should take note. The GLA’s cabin is short on space for people and cargo, but it offers sophisticated styling and lots of high-tech features and options. Buyers seeking traditional crossover practicality and roominess would be wise to shop the BMW X1 or the Lexus NX—but the GLA-class is far more entertaining to drive.
What's New for 2018?
A mild freshening highlights the GLA-class for 2018. Updated front and rear bumpers, wheel designs, LED taillamps, and grille enhance its already distinctive exterior styling. Inside, new chrome trim sparkles on the center console and door panels, there's a larger 8.0-inch infotainment screen, and the gauge cluster has a more legible black background. In addition, a backup camera and a foot-activated liftgate are now standard.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing
Original MSRP:
- GLA250: $34,395
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
Turbocharged power, a slick-shifting transmission, sporty suspension, and available all-wheel drive give the GLA250 hot-hatchback performance at the test track. The turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine makes 208 hp and mates to a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Buyers looking for a plush, easygoing crossover should look elsewhere—the GLA250 blends more athleticism into its chassis than many rivals, which should appeal to enthusiasts. Its handling is sharp and athletic, but when pushed to the limit, the GLA250 is quick to remind you that you’re not behind the wheel of a sports car. And its firm suspension results in a rough ride over uneven roads.
Fuel Economy
EPA fuel-economy testing and reporting procedures have changed over time. For the latest numbers on current and older vehicles, visit the EPA’s website and select Find & Compare Cars.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
A tight back seat, small rear window, and un-Mercedes-like touches plague the GLA250’s interior. Overall, the design is stylish and sophisticated, the controls are easy to reach, and the metal trim and faux leather are pleasing. Standard features include power front seats, dual-zone climate control, and a power liftgate. And there are plenty of packages and options to allow personalization. But some of the material finishes and panel fit are less refined than what we’d expect from a Mercedes-Benz. As with passenger space, cargo room in the GLA250 is limited. There's enough capacity for the casual user, but those looking for maximum space should check out the BMW X1. Small cubbies and bins are sprinkled throughout the interior, but none of them is large enough to be useful.
Infotainment and Connectivity
We found the GLA250's COMAND infotainment system to be intuitive and useful. The GLA-class comes standard with such features as an 8.0-inch infotainment screen, Bluetooth connectivity, an eight-speaker stereo, and two USB ports. Options include navigation, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Wi-Fi, a premium Harman Kardon audio system, and SiriusXM satellite radio.
Safety Features and Crash Test Ratings
For more information about the Mercedes-Benz GLA-class’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

title: 2019 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
2019 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class
- Enthusiastic chassis, available high-tech features, distinctive styling.
- Undersize cargo space, stiff ride, cramped rear seat.
- While it doesn't feel as luxurious as its Benz big brothers, its peppy performance and nimble handling make it fun to drive.

Overview
Consider the 2019 Mercedes-Benz GLA-class a hot hatch for 401k-contributing adults: It's kind of a crossover and kind of a performance hatchback. Underneath its ruggedly styled sheetmetal it's basically a CLA-class sedan. Its performance-oriented driving characteristics remind us more of a hot hatchback than anything else, and enthusiast drivers should take note. The GLA's cabin is short on space for people and cargo, but it offers high-tech options such as Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and 4G LTE connectivity with onboard Wi-Fi. Buyers seeking traditional crossover practicality and roominess would be wise to shop the BMW X1 and the Lexus NX, but the GLA-class is far more entertaining to drive.
What's New for 2019?
Mercedes-Benz's smallest crossover holds steady for 2019 with only one change: A new Iridium Silver paint color joins the options list. Mercedes has been busy revamping its small car lineup in the form of the all-new A-class and CLA-class sedans, so an all-new GLA-class can't be far behind.

Pricing and Which One to Buy
