Overview
The Mercedes-Benz EQE sedan is quiet, smooth-riding, luxurious, and—with up to 308 miles of EPA-estimated range—good on electrons. The trouble is, the same can be said of pretty much every other electric luxury sedan, and many of those models have two things that the EQE doesn’t: an engaging driving personality and attractive looks. At least its nondescript shape does an excellent job of helping it slip through the air with minimal aerodynamic drag.
The EQE comes in single-motor rear-drive or twin-motor all-wheel drive configurations. While both setups have an identical 315 ponies, torque leaps up by some 36 percent with two motors. We have nice things to say about the interior, which features plush seats, beautiful materials, and chic design. Mercedes apparently agrees with our tepid response to its mid-size luxury EV sedan: it's rumored to be up for replacement in 2027 with something more competitive to the likes of the Lucid Air and BMW i5.
Expert Tip: Not surprisingly, Mercedes offers this electric sedan in AMG form, and in high-performance guise, it does deliver some serious performance for its six-figure asking price.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#11 in Best Luxury Electric CarsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
To help the EQE live out its days, for 2026 it aims to tempt consumers with a 27-hp boost, a standard NACS adapter, and fresh wheel options. Moreover, Benz has downgraded the model’s number badge from 350 to 320 for reasons we’ve yet to uncover and has eliminated the 402-hp EQE500 from the lineup.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
- EV Motors: 315-hp single motor, 315-hp dual motor
- Drivetrains: rear-wheel drive, all-wheel drive
Two models make up the 2026 EQE lineup: the single-motor, rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ and the plus-less EQE320 4Matic, featuring all-wheel drive and two motors. The presence of the second motor doesn’t affect horsepower—both cars make 315 ponies—but it does increase torque considerably, from 416 pound-feet to 564.
We’ve yet to take the revised EQE sedan for a spin, but we expect it’ll behave much like the previous 350s: sedately. The ride in the EQEs that we've previously sampled proved calm and quiet, thanks to their optional adaptive air-spring suspensions, but even with the optional rear-wheel-steering system, this EV isn’t a dynamic marvel. It feels quick enough, but is less satisfying to drive than rivals such as the BMW i5 and the Lucid Air.
0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Test: 5.3 seconds (EQE350 4Matic)
In Comparison: Compared with most other vehicles on the road today, the EQE is respectably quick, but among luxury electric sedans, it’s behind on pace. The base, rear-drive Lucid Air Pure, for instance, hits 60 in just 4.3 seconds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- C/D Range Test: 260 miles (EQE350 4Matic)
- Claimed EV Range: 267-308 miles
The EPA says that the rear-drive model is good for 308 miles with its 96.0-kWh battery fully charged. The 4Matic car, which has a 90.5-kWh battery, lasts for a claimed 267 miles. In our hands on the highway, a 2023 EQE350 4Matic nearly met that range estimate, going for 260 miles.
Both models, according to Mercedes, have a maximum charging rate of 170 kilowatts and require just over a half-hour on a DC fast-charger to restore their battery charge from 10 to 80 percent. On a Level 2 station, the EQE320+ needs 11.5 hours, whereas the EQE320 4Matic requires 10.8.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
- C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 67 MPGe (EQE350 4Matic)
- EPA City Ratings: 87-94 MPGe
- EPA Highway Ratings: 85-94 MPGe
According to the EPA, the EQE320+ earns estimates of 94 MPGe city and 94 MPGe highway; the 4Matic comes in at 87 MPGe city and 85 MPGe highway. (MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV fuel efficiency.)
On our real-world, 75-mph fuel-economy route, the previous EQE350 4Matic saw only 67 MPGe. For more information about the EQE's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: The EQE cabin is elegant and well put together. Cushy heated seats await the driver and front passenger; shoppers can splurge for ventilation and massage functions too. The standard panoramic glass roof helps provide a sense of airiness.
Second Row: The EQE's skateboard-like electric platform is a boon to packaging, providing comfortable passenger accommodations in the back.
Cargo Capacity: The EV offers an adequate amount of trunk space and plenty of storage spots inside the cabin, including a pass-through cubby in the center console.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 12.8-inch touchscreen (standard), 17.7-inch touchscreen (optional)
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio Systems: 9-speaker Burmester stereo (standard), 15-speaker Burmester stereo (optional)
The 12.8-inch touchscreen runs on the MBUX software, supports wireless smartphone-mirroring tech, and responds to taps, voice commands, and steering-wheel-button inputs. There’s also a biometric sensor that allows owners to access saved settings via a finger scan. Navigation is provided, though Benz’s augmented-reality enhancements cost extra (and need a little work).
Shoppers can also spec the brand’s Hyperscreen infotainment system, which combines the 12.3-inch instrument panel with a 17.7-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch passenger display under a single piece of glass that spans the dash and looks futuristic.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Mercedes provides a suite of driver-assistance technology on the EQE sedan, though it requires shoppers to pay extra for adaptive cruise control.
- Standard Safety Features: lane-keeping assist, automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring
- Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control, evasive-steering assist
For information about the EQE’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes-Benz’s limited and powertrain warranties are in line with what other luxury automakers offer. However, unlike BMW, it doesn't provide any complimentary maintenance.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Battery-Component Warranty: eight years or 155,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

title: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
- Home
- Mercedes-Benz
- GLC-Class EV
2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV
- Impressive range estimates, luxurious interior, comfortable highway ride.
- Big-mouth grille might not be for everyone, overwhelming array of on-screen technology.
- The electric version of the GLC forges its own path with distinct styling, a high-tech interior, and strong range and acceleration performance.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV for sale near ?
Overview
It looks a lot like the regular gasoline-powered GLC-class SUV, but the electric powertrain hiding under the sheetmetal sets the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-class EV on an entirely different journey. We’ve had a chance to drive the new compact electric crossover, and its ride is smooth, its powertrain is perky, and its luxury experience is intact.
Two models will be offered—the single-motor GLC300+ and the dual-motor, all-wheel-drive GLC400 4Matic—and both come with the same battery pack. Driving range for the GLC400 should be around 380 miles per charge, says Mercedes, but we don't know yet what the range will be for the GLC300+. Both are spacious, upscale, and tech-forward, especially the models with the large 39.1-inch Hyperscreen that spans the full width of the dash.
Expert Tip: If you aren't ready to leap into all-electric SUV ownership, Mercedes-Benz currently sells a plug-in hybrid version of the gas-powered GLC. We review that model separately.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#5 in Best Electric Compact Luxury SUVsCompare the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2027?
The GLC-Class EV is a new addition to the Mercedes-Benz lineup. It slots in under the mid-size EQE SUV, and its naming convention marks a move away from the EQ prefix that Benz has used on its EVs so far.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
- EV Motors: 369-hp single motor, 483-hp dual motor
- Drivetrains: rear-wheel-drive, all-wheel-drive
The base GLC300+ gets a single electric motor that makes 369 horsepower and drives the rear wheels. All-wheel drive is available by upgrading to the dual-motor GLC400 4Matic, which offers a combined 483 horsepower.
A two-speed automatic transmission is onboard, but you don’t feel it shifting gears. Ride comfort is good, especially on the optional air-spring suspension system, which can also raise the GLC EV for more ground clearance should you decide to venture off-road.
0–60-MPH Times
- Claimed 60-mph Time: 5.9 seconds (manufacturer estimate, GLC300+), 4.0 seconds (C/D estimate, GLC400 4Matic)
In Comparison: The GLC-Class EV's primary rivals are the BMW iX3 and the Porsche Macan EV, and while the iX3's 60 mph estimate is close to that of the GLC400's at 4.7 seconds, the Macan EV 4S we tested managed to be quicker at 3.6 seconds to 60.
Towing and Payload Capacity
- Max Towing: 5291 pounds
A trailer hitch is an optional extra, and Mercedes says that with it installed, the GLC400 model can tow up to 5291 pounds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- Estimated EV Range: 380 miles
Based on Mercedes-Benz's range predictions for the GLC400 4Matic model, we expect its EPA range estimate will come in at around 380 miles. The company hasn't revealed an estimated range for the single-motor GLC300+.
The GLC EV can charge its 94-kWh battery pack at up to 400-volt charging stations, which Mercedes-Benz claims results in adding 188 miles of charge in just 10 minutes. We look forward to testing this claim when we get our hands on an electric GLC.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: Premium materials are used throughout the GLC EV's cabin, but it feels like there are too many screens and lighting elements. The overall look inside, especially when equipped with the optional Hyperscreen dashboard setup, is overwhelmingly digital. That said, the front seat area is comfortable and spacious, with plenty of storage cubbies and supportive bucket seats.
Second Row: The GLC EV's back seat is roomier than its gas-powered sibling. There's plenty of legroom, and even tall adults should fit just fine.
Cargo Capacity: The rear cargo bay is spacious too, at 20.1 cubic feet, which should be more than enough for a weekend's worth of luggage or a family-sized grocery haul. If you need more space, there's also a 4.5 cubic-foot front trunk.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 14.0-inch touchscreen (standard), 39.1-inch Hyperscreen (optional)
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Audio System: 5-speaker stereo (standard), 16-speaker Burmester stereo
A 14.0-inch touchscreen with a separate digital gauge display is standard, but the optional 39.1-inch Hyperscreen is more buzzworthy and makes the dashboard almost entirely digital. Navigation, Bluetooth, and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are all standard.
A 5-speaker stereo is standard fare, but a 16-speaker Burmester setup is optional and features Dolby Atmos spatial audio technology. SiriusXM satellite radio is included with all models.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Mercedes-Benz includes many driver-assistance features as standard, but to unlock the most advanced tech, you'll need to add MB.Drive Assist Plus or MB.Drive Assist Pro.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot warning
- Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control with a hands-free driving mode
For information about the GLC-Class EV's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes' warranty periods align with other luxury automakers, such as Audi and BMW. However, unlike those German competitors, Benz-branded models don't include any complimentary maintenance.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- EV Component Warranty:10 years or 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: None

title: 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Beth Nichols
text:
- Home
- Mercedes-Benz
- GLA-Class
2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class
- Handsome styling, upscale interior, comfortable ride and handling.
- Unremarkable acceleration, short on standard features, rivals are more fun to drive.
- The little GLA earns our admiration for its smooth personality, quiet engine, and luxe cabin, but it is not a car that stirs the soul.

Overview
The Mercedes-Benz GLA250 is a good-looking, easy-to-drive contender in the subcompact luxury SUV class. It can’t quite match the driving joy of BMW’s X1or X2, but it doesn’t embarrass itself on twisty tarmac either, and its turbocharged four-cylinder provides sufficient and hushed motivation for your daily driving needs.
The cabin is well-appointed and spacious considering the GLA’s diminutive size. Not surprisingly, given the three-pointed star on its nose, its starting price is a little higher than that of the Volvo XC40 and Audi Q3. Benz squeezes customers for more, making features like adaptive cruise control, proximity keyless entry, and heated front seats optional. A GLA can get pricey quick if you load it up with amenities like a head-up display or built-in navigation.
Expert Tip: Want a GLA that can kick it up a couple of notches? Look at the hot-rodded, 302-hp Mercedes-AMG GLA35. It too lacks standard features, but it's a seriously fun (and expensive) version of this subcompact SUV.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#11 in Best Subcompact Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
A no-cost AMG Lite Plus Package is now available for the GLA-class, which adds a bit of flair to the SUV's exterior styling. The package includes 19-inch AMG wheels and a rear spoiler. A Midnight Edition is also new, which features 20-inch AMG wheels and blacked-out trim. The only other addition is a new $1500 Sun and Sound package, which bundles a panoramic sunroof with the upgraded 10-speaker Advanced sound system.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
- Engine: 221-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder
- Transmission: 8-speed dual-clutch automatic
- Drivetrains: front-wheel drive, all-wheel drive
The GLA-class's turbo-four revs smoothly. As of the 2024 model year, the crossover makes use of a 48-volt hybrid system, which helps reduce turbo lag for more response off the line, among other things. We’ve yet to sample a model with this tech, but we don’t expect the GLA’s performance numbers to change because of it.
As for how the GLA250drives, it's composed over rough stretches but comports itself with confidence when the road squirms; we like its precise steering, though you won't mistake it for a high-performance machine.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Test: 6.3 seconds (AWD)
In Comparison: At our test track, the GLA250's performance proved adequate but far from quick. While its acceleration is in league with the Volvo XC40's, it can't keep up with the BMW X1, which posted a 5.4-second 60-mph time.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
- EPA City Ratings: 25-26 mpg
- EPA Highway Ratings: 33-34 mpg
The EPA states that the front-wheel-drive model earns estimates of 26 mpg city and 34 mpg highway, while the 4Matic all-wheel drive system drops those figures to 25 and 33 mpg, respectively. These numbers are pretty good for a subcompact SUV.
We haven't had a chance to test a GLA250 on our highway fuel-economy route, but we’ll update this page with the results when we do. For more information about the GLA’s fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: For a subcompact SUV, the GLA is relatively spacious and comfortable inside, and the cabin looks suitably upscale and modern. Leatherette and carbon-fiber trim come standard, though Benz offers leather upholstery and more premium accent materials (such as aluminum and wood) for those who care to spend more. Seat heating also costs extra.
Second Row: The Benz’s second row offers more rear-seat legroom than its top competitors, including the Audi Q3, BMW X1, and Volvo XC40. Two adults fit without issue.
Cargo Capacity: The GLA is far from a leader in cargo capacity, but the load floor is flush with the rear hatch's sill, which makes it easy to slide in large and heavy items. In our testing, the GLA250 managed to fit six carry-on suitcases behind its rear seat, matching the Q3.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 10.3-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio Systems: 6-speaker stereo (standard), 10-speaker stereo (optional), 12-speaker Burmester stereo (optional)
Every GLA is equipped with two 10.3-inch screens united behind a single glass panel spanning more than half the dash. One is for the driver's gauge display, and the other controls the infotainment system, which runs the latest version of the brand’s MBUX software. Users can issue voice commands, tap steering-wheel buttons, or hit icons on the screen to adjust settings and make selections. They can also wirelessly connect to the Apple CarPlay or Android Auto interface.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Automated emergency braking and high-beam assist are standard, but shoppers interested in more advanced driver-assistance features such as adaptive cruise control and lane-keeping assist will need to pay extra.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, automatic high-beams, blind-spot monitoring
- Optional Safety Features: lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, evasive-steering assist
For information about the GLA’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes offers typical warranty terms, with coverage stretching four years or 50,000 miles. The Lexus NX can better that, and rival models made by BMW and Volvo receive lengthy contracts for complimentary scheduled maintenance.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles

title: 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Beth Nichols
text:
2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV
- Excellent fit and finish, respectable range estimates, fairly quick.
- Has some unflattering angles, lacks physical buttons, dynamically disappointing.
- The EQS SUV has the opulence, tech, and passenger space to earn its spot at the top of Mercedes-Benz's electric lineup.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV for sale near 04347
312–317 Miles
5 Seats
Electric
All-Wheel Drive
4 Years/50,000 Miles
Overview
With space for up to seven, the Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV is an electric people-hauler with first-class accommodations and a bevy of slick features. Every rider is surrounded by leather, wood, glass, and—most importantly—space. The Hyperscreen dashboard is sure to impress anyone at first glance, too, though owners may come to find the all-touchscreen interface tiring, as we did.
All-wheel drive is standard, and both available models make good use of their two-motor powertrains.
The lineup-topping 536-hp EQS550 4Matic hits 60 in a brisk 4.0 seconds and travels up to 317 miles on a charge, while the much less expensive EQS400 4Matic boasts a 5.2-second sprint and a 312-mile range. The experience behind the wheel is pleasurable but not thrilling. The SUV's rear-axle steering helps with tight turns and high-speed stability, and the adaptive suspension adequately dampens bumps in the road, but neither makes this heavy EV playful.
Expert Tip: Enthusiasts will likely be happier in the BMW iX or Rivian R1S.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#17 in Best Electric Mid-Size Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
The rear-drive EQS450+ is gone, and last year's 4Matic models—the EQS450 and EQS580—are now the EQS400 and EQS550 despite receiving no discernable powertrain changes.
In other news, Benz improved the SUV's standard-features list. Every model now boasts a NACS adapter (for use at Tesla Supercharger stations) and an upgraded second row with seat heating, a wireless charging pad, fancy pillowed headrests, and rear side airbags.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
EV Motor, Power, and Performance
- EV Motors: 355-hp dual motors, 536-hp dual motors
- Drivetrain: all-wheel drive
The EQS SUV is essentially a re-bodied EQS sedan with an elevated seating position and more interior space. The rear-drive, single-motor model is off the table for 2026, but the all-wheel-drive (4Matic) SUVs live on with new badge numbers. The EQS400 4Matic makes 355 horsepower and 590 pound-feet of torque from its two motors, while the EQS550 4Matic produces a total of 536 horsepower and 633 pound-feet.
All EQS SUVs come with an adjustable air suspension and a rear-axle-steering system that makes the big people-mover surprisingly easy to maneuver. Handling is capable but not particularly satisfying, and steering feedback is minimal.
Unlike the EQS sedan, the SUV features an Off-Road drive mode that raises the suspension and alters the powertrain's behavior. During a ride-along in a prototype, we experienced this setting on rugged terrain and were impressed with the vehicle's capabilities. The 2026 EQS400 SUV we drove had relaxed and comfortable on-road demeanor, which is okay by us given its luxury mission.
0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Tests: 5.2 seconds (EQS400 4Matic)
In our testing, the 2026 EQS400 4Matic recorded a 60-mph time of 5.2 seconds. The previous EQS580 4Matic we tested, which is mechanically identical to the current EQS550 4Matic, recorded a 4.0-second blast to 60 mph.
In Comparison: Output ratings in this class vary considerably, which makes comparison tricky. A two-motor Genesis GV60 Performance operating at 483 horsepower gets to 60 in 3.7 seconds, while a 500-hp all-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriq needs 4.6 seconds to reach that speed.
Towing and Payload Capacity
- Max Towing: 3500 pounds
The EQS SUV can tow up to 3500 pounds when properly equipped.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- C/D Range Tests: 290 miles (2023 EQS450 4Matic and EQS580 4Matic)
- EPA EV Range: 312-317 miles
The 2026 EQS SUVs wield a 118-kWh battery pack that's good for 312 miles of range in the EQS400 4Matic and 317 miles in the more powerful EQS550 4Matic. Both models support DC fast-charging at a rate of up to 200 kilowatts, which will restore the battery’s charge from 10 to 80 percent in about half an hour. In our testing, we were able to charge from 10 percent to 90 percent in 43 minutes.
On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test route, the 2023 EQS450 4Matic and the EQS580 4Matic both delivered 290 miles of range. We'll update this page with results for the latest models when we get the chance to test them.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
- C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Tests: 78 MPGe (2023 EQS450 4Matic), 83 MPGe (2023 EQS580 4Matic)
- EPA City Ratings: 80-82 MPGe
- EPA Highway Rating: 78 MPGe
The EPA rates the 2026 EQS450 4Matic at 80 MPGe city and 78 MPGe highway, while the EQS580 gets 82 and 78 MPGe, respectively. (MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV fuel efficiency.)
On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy route, 2023 versions of the EQS450 4Matic and EQS580 4Matic—which employ slightly smaller battery packs than the current models—saw 78 MPGe and 83 MPGe. For more information about the EQS SUV's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: Inside, the EQS SUV features the type of rich materials and high-tech equipment that define modern-day Mercedes-Benz models. User-adjustable ambient lighting, heated and ventilated front seats, lush leather upholstery, a panoramic sunroof, Benz's dash-spanning Hyperscreen, and wireless charging are included.
Second Row: Riders in the second row have ample leg- and headroom, not to mention standard seat heating, wireless phone charging, and luxury headrests.
Third Row: A two-seat third row is available and suitable for adults on short trips. The SUV's sloping roofline eats into headroom, though.
Cargo Capacity: The cabin has several storage spaces, including a large bin below the floating center console. Cargo volume varies by seat count, with five-seaters offering 31 cubic feet behind the second row and seven-seaters, 28. With all three rows up, cargo capacity drops to just seven cubic feet. In our testing, a two-row EQS SUV held 10 carry-on suitcases in its cargo bay, and a total of 24 with the second-row seats folded.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 17.7-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio System: 15-speaker Burmester stereo
For maximum theater, the EQS SUV is equipped with Mercedes's mesmerizing 56-inch Hyperscreen, which spans the dash from door to door. Along with housing the digital gauge cluster, it hosts a 17.7-inch touchscreen that's primarily responsible for infotainment functions, plus a 12.3-inch touchscreen in front of the passenger. There's no doubt that the novelty of the glass-covered dash will entice buyers, but we can't help but bemoan the near-total lack of easy-to-use physical switchgear. Every EQS SUV also comes standard with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, a Burmester audio system, and wireless device charging.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The EQS SUV has a host of standard driver-assistance technology. Along with ordinary safety equipment, such as adaptive cruise control and automatic high-beam headlamps, the SUV also has a self-parking feature.
- Standard Safety Features: lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring
For information about the EQS SUV’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Mercedes's warranty periods align with those of other luxury automakers, such as Audi and BMW. However, unlike those German competitors, Benz-branded models don't include any complimentary maintenance.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Battery-Component Warranty: 10 years or 155,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

2026 Mercedes-Benz C-Class
- Classic luxury-sedan styling, luxe and comfy cabin, agile handling.
- Numb steering, overly firm ride, some brake-pedal squishiness.
- The C-class is more successful as a luxury car than a sports sedan, though it attempts to be both.

Overview
Given its price point, the Mercedes-Benz C-class does a surprisingly good job of imitating the much larger and pricier S-class. Its interior is comfortable, modern, and well-built with top-notch materials, and it has the classic proportions of an old-school luxury sedan.
The C-class is not as refined as Mercedes's flagship sedan, of course, and while it's nimble and reasonably powerful, its suspension tune and steering system could use more work. Still, it’s a solid choice for anyone shopping for an entry-level luxury car.
Expert Tip: If the C300 is too tame, there are performance-oriented AMG versions available: The C43 makes 416 horsepower, while the plug-in-hybrid C63churns out 671 ponies.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#5 in Best Compact Luxury CarsCompare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz C-Class with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
A new AMG Lite Plus Package is now available for the C-class, which adds a bit of flair to the sedan's exterior styling. The package includes 19-inch AMG wheels, a panoramic sunroof, and a rear spoiler. The 19-inch wheels are offered outside of the package at no additional cost. The Night Package, which adds gloss black exterior elements, is now a $400 standalone package that is no longer included with the AMG Line Package. Inside the cabin, a new Black Fine Structure center console material is available, and surround view functionality is now available as a standalone option.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

Engine, Transmission, and Performance
- Engine: 255-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder
- Transmission: 9-speed automatic
- Drivetrains: rear-wheel drive, all-wheel drive
All C-class models employ a 255-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder enhanced by a 48-volt hybrid system that can temporarily boost power at low rpm. A nine-speed automatic transmission and rear-wheel drive are standard, though Benz will fit its 4Matic all-wheel-drive system for more coin.
The C’s handling is nimble, but the ride is somewhat flinty, and the steering is lifeless. At least this sedan brakes with vigor, stopping from 70 mph in just 154 feet. Pedal feel could be firmer, though.

- C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 35 mpg (C300 4Matic AWD)
- EPA City Rating: 24-25 mpg
- EPA Highway Rating: 33-35 mpg
The rear-wheel-drive C300 model earns EPA fuel-economy estimates of 25 mpg city and 35 mpg highway. All-wheel-drive C300 4Matic models do a little worse in each cycle, with ratings of 24 and 33 mpg, respectively.
In our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test, the C300 4Matic beat its highway rating with a 35-mpg result. For more information about the C-class's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: The C300’s cabin looks high-tech and suitably luxurious, with a digital gauge display, touch-sensitive controls, and a host of amenities such as heated front seats with memory settings, a sunroof, open-pore wood trim, and aluminum accents. Fit and finish is also excellent.
Second Row: For a compact car, the C300 has a roomy second row. Adults should be fine back there for hour-long rides.
Cargo Capacity: Though the Benz’s cargo volume is merely adequate for the class, Mercedes installs handy seat-dropping buttons in the trunk so owners can easily free up more storage space as needed. In our testing, we fit six carry-on suitcases in the trunk, and a total of 15 cases with the rear seats folded down.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 11.9-inch touchscreen
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility
- Audio Systems: 5-speaker stereo (standard), 15-speaker Burmester stereo (optional)
A portrait-oriented, driver-facing 11.9-inch touchscreen is standard in every C-class. The display runs the third-gen MBUX infotainment system, which supports a voice-activated digital assistant, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto functions, and a Wi-Fi hotspot.
A 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster and wireless device charging are also included, while a head-up display and a 15-speaker Burmester surround-sound stereo are optional.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Mercedes equips the C-class with some useful driver-assistance features, but the best tech—like the adaptive-cruise-control system that utilizes GPS data to adjust the vehicle's speed for upcoming curves and roundabouts—is optional.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, automated parking tech
- Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, lane-departure warning
For information about the C-class’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
New C300s come with rival-matching warranty coverage but no complimentary maintenance (whereas competitor cars from BMW, Genesis, and Volvo offer three years of scheduled service).

- Powertrain Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: none

title: 2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Austin Parsons
text:
2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class
- Playful chassis, all seats suitable for adults, extra EV operation over other hybrids.
- Awkward powertrain handoffs, EV motor needs more juice, some cheap interior bits.
- The CLA's new hybrid powertrain lacks refinement, giving buyers a compelling reason to check out the electric version.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA-class for sale near 200000
Overview
The CLA-class has served as Mercedes-Benz's starter sedan for over a decade, and it's about to enter its third generation with updated styling and a new hybrid powertrain. As part of an expanding lineup, the reworked 48-volt hybrid variants will enter the picture after the release of two new electric CLA models, which we review separately. The hybrid CLA will be offered as a CLA220 model with either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. With its modernized fastback styling and fresh hybrid setup, the new CLA-class is poised to take the fight to its subcompact competition including the Audi A3 and the BMW 2-Series Gran Coupe.
What's New for 2027?
The CLA-class enters its third generation with some major updates. Mercedes-Benz has developed an entirely new platform for the forthcoming CLA, which will also provide the basis for a pair of small SUVs, as well as a station-wagon CLA variant. The CLA retains its egglike fastback silhouette, but with contemporary front- and rear-end styling that incorporates the Mercedes-Benz star motif into the headlights and taillights. Its hybrid powertrain is entirely new, combining a freshly developed turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder gas engine with a redesigned 48-volt hybrid system. The hybrid CLA variants are also joined by an electric CLA model.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
The 2027 Mercedes CLA will use a new turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine with a 48-volt hybrid system. The U.S. version is available as a CLA220 model with 208 horsepower and either front- or all-wheel drive. The hybrid system features a 1.3-kWh battery and a 30-hp electric motor that is incorporated into a new version of Benz's eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The electrified transmission can be decoupled from the engine, allowing the car to run on electric power alone for very short distances. During our test drive, we found the handoff between electric power and gasoline power to be rough; selecting Sport mode helps somewhat because it keeps the gas engine running and uses the electric motor as a boost. The CLA's handling is pleasant, though, and it has nicely weighted steering.
0–60-MPH Times
We estimate that the CLA Hybrid will get to 60 mph in around 6.8 seconds. The electric version is likely to be quicker.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
The EPA hasn't yet released any fuel economy figures for the new CLA-class hybrid, but we estimate it will be rated at around 38 mpg combined. We'll update this story when EPA figures roll in and we have a chance to take the CLA on our 75-mph highway fuel economy test route.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
The CLA's interior blends hypermodern design with classy touches. While its massive digital gauge display and infotainment screen dominate the front cabin, brushed aluminum detailing and plush leather upholstery keep the interior looking elegant. The new CLA's slightly larger exterior dimensions translate to the interior, which offers slightly more legroom and headroom than the outgoing model.
Infotainment and Connectivity
Interior tech was clearly a priority for the new CLA, as the dashboard is dedicated almost entirely to digital real estate. A 10.3-inch digital gauge display and 14-inch central infotainment touchscreen come standard. An optional cabin-spanning display (dubbed the MBUX Superscreen by Mercedes) adds an additional 14-inch passenger screen to the already sizable infotainment setup. The CLA's infotainment, navigation, and driver assistance systems use Merc's new MB.OS operating system, which adds features like over-the-air software updates and a new AI-based virtual assistant.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Driver-assistance features, such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automated emergency braking, are all standard on the CLA. For more information about the CLA-class's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features are likely to include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection
- Standard lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Available adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
The warranty coverage provided by the Mercedes-Benz CLA-class matches the protection offered by competing cars from brands such as BMW and Audi.
- Limited warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance

title: 2026 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Drew Dorian
text:
2026 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid
- Premium look and feel, compliant ride, fuel-efficient powertrain.
- Forgettable handling dynamics, expensive starting price, more electric range would be nice.
- The Corsair Hybrid marries luxury and fuel efficiency in an agreeable package.
For Sale Near You

Hybrid
All-Wheel Drive

Overview
Lincoln's most fuel-efficient offering is the 2026 Corsair Hybrid, which takes the standard Corsair model, juices it up with a little more power, and adds a plug. The plug-in hybrid powertrain combines a four-cylinder gas engine with two electric motors for a total of 266 horsepower. Performance and handling aren't anything to celebrate here, but the Lincoln's well-cushioned ride will win favor with drivers who prioritize comfort. The Corsair Hybrid's onboard battery pack holds enough juice for up to 27 miles of electric range, but extracting that many miles requires careful driving. It's better to just drive the Corsair Hybrid casually and enjoy the comfortable seats, which can be optioned as 24-way power-adjustable thrones with massage.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#4 in Best Hybrid Compact Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
Lincoln has made no changes to the Corsair Hybrid for 2026.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
The Lincoln Corsair Grand Touring pairs a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gas engine with two electric motors for a total system output of 266 horsepower; that's 16 horses more than you get from the Corsair's standard turbocharged 2.0-liter four. Power from the gas engine is delivered through a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) and all-wheel drive comes standard. While the Corsair Grand Touring is adequately quick for day-to-day driving, rival PHEV crossovers are quicker. The GT exhibits similar road manners to the nonhybrid, complete with a pillowy ride and uninspired steering feel.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
0–60-MPH Times
At our test track, the PHEV model managed to reach 60 mph in 6.2 seconds, which is just 0.1 second behind the nonhybrid model.
Towing and Payload Capacity
The Corsair Hybrid is rated to tow up to 2000 pounds. That's less than the nonhybrid model, which can tow up to 3000 pounds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
Thanks to its 14.4-kWh battery, the Corsair Grand Touring can travel up to 27 miles on electric power alone—as long as you go easy on the right pedal. Prod it too hard in EV mode, and the gas engine will fire up for assistance. In our real-world 75-mph highway range test, we achieved 19 miles on a full charge. By toggling to the Preserve EV mode, the GT uses the gas power plant and regenerative braking to maintain the battery’s charge for later use. When the pack is depleted, Lincoln says it takes about 10 to 11 hours to recharge via a standard 110-volt outlet and three to four hours from a 240-volt outlet.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
The EPA estimates fuel economy for the Corsair Grand Touring at 34 mpg city, 32 mpg highway, and 33 mpg combined. In our real-world 75-mph highway fuel economy test, we achieved 53 MPGe in EV mode and 31 mpg in hybrid mode. That puts the Corsair Grand Touring squarely mid-pack among its peers, including the more efficient Lexus NX450h+ and less efficient Volvo XC60 T8 Recharge. MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV vehicle fuel efficiency. For more information about the Corsair Grand Touring’s fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
The Corsair boasts a handsome cabin that's similar to those in other SUV offerings from Lincoln, such as the Navigator, Nautilus, and Aviator. It's upholstered in soft leather and offers plenty of features. Adjustable ambient lighting, 24-way power-adjustable seats, a head-up display, and an app that allows users to unlock, lock, and start the vehicle with their smartphone are all available—although ordering such items will add a princely sum to the bottom line. Surprisingly, Lincoln says a top-spec Black Label model of the Corsair is not in the cards. The Corsair's cargo bay is generously sized. We managed to fit eight carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats. Lowering the rear seatbacks opens up enough room for 21 cases in total.
Infotainment and Connectivity
A 13.2-inch infotainment display running Lincoln’s most up-to-date software is standard, and a 12.3-inch digital gauge display also comes on every model. Although there is a bit of a learning curve, the interface is easy to use, with joysticks on the steering wheel and voice-activated navigation helping the driver avoid reaching for the screen too often. The Grand Touring features a standard Revel 14-speaker audio system that comes with SiriusXM along with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
The Corsair hybrid comes standard with a suite of driver-assistance features that Lincoln calls Co-Pilot360, but unlocking high-tech assists such as a self-parking feature or a hands-free driving mode called BlueCruise requires springing for an option package. For more information about the Corsair hybrid’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Standard lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Standard adaptive cruise control
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Lincoln's standard powertrain warranty is more generous than its German rivals. Buyers of nonhybrid Black Label models are treated to a four-year/50,000-mile complimentary scheduled maintenance plan, but because the Corsair isn't offered in the Black Label trim, its buyers will have to go out of pocket for all oil changes, tire rotations, and the like.
- Limited warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers six years or 70,000 miles
- Hybrid components are covered for eight years or 100,000 miles
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance

title: 2026 Lexus RX Hybrid Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Eric Stafford
text:
2026 Lexus RX Hybrid
- Passenger-pampering ride, calming cabin atmosphere, PHEV now a lot more affordable.
- Looks sporty but isn't, 350h powertrain is forgettable, PHEV is the priciest but not the quickest.
- The Lexus RX Hybrid prioritizes comfort, efficiency, and style but skips the fun stuff.

All-Wheel Drive

Overview
Some people prefer a calm, comforting driving experience over an exciting one. People who feel that way will appreciate the Lexus RX Hybrid, which puts those traits and a stylish appearance at the top of the list. Lexus's compact luxury SUV also features a trio of fuel-sipping powertrains that help stretch a gallon of gas, especially the plug-in hybrid model, which is now more affordable.
No matter what RX you choose, a cushy ride and serene cabin are primary ingredients. There are only two rows of seats, and those sitting up front have easy access to a user-friendly infotainment system. While the gas-electric RX feels more subdued than, say, the BMW X3 or the Porsche Macan, it can look the part with the brand's available F Sport treatments.
Expert Tip: If you want the same sleek styling and similarly luxurious interior for a lower price, check out the nonhybrid Lexus RX, which starts at $51,175 and features a 275-hp turbo four.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#3 in Best Hybrid Compact Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Lexus RX Hybrid with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
For 2026, the RX Hybrid lineup doesn't receive any significant aesthetic or mechanical changes, though there are some noteworthy updates. The plug-in hybrid is still the most expensive variant, but a new Premium trim notably lowers the cost of entry; its $66,680 starting price is almost $6K less than last year. For those who opt for the F Sport Handling or F Sport Performance treatments, they're now compatible with the Appearance package (black 21-inch wheels, black exterior add-ons, orange brake calipers). Finally, you no longer must pay extra for wireless phone charging, as it's now standard across the lineup.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Lexus RX Hybrid to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
- Hybrid Powertrains: 2.4-liter four-cylinder and three electric motors, 246 hp combined; turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder and two electric motors, 366 hp combined; 2.5-liter four-cylinder and three electric motors, 304 hp combined
- Transmission: continuously variable automatic transmission
- Drivetrain: all-wheel drive
The regular RX350h's powertrain felt sluggish when we drove it, and we estimate it will deliver slightly slower acceleration than its predecessor. Stepping up to the RX500h F Sport Performance unlocks a punchier powertrain, but while Lexus had an opportunity to recast the current-generation RX as a performer with the RX500h model, its chassis engineers regrettably chose not to dial in any additional cornering confidence. All models we've driven so far are just as softly sprung and focused on luxury as the previous-generation RX. That will please faithful buyers but is unlikely to attract driving enthusiasts. A plug-in hybrid model, the RX450h+, features the same powertrain that's offered in the Lexus NX450h+ subcompact SUV, but it makes two extra horsepower in this application, bringing the total to 304 ponies.
What's Your Car Worth?

0–60-MPH Times
- C/D 60-mph Test: 5.5 seconds (RX500h F Sport), 6.0 seconds (RX450h+ Luxury)
We haven't had the chance to test an RX350h yet, but when we do, we'll update this story with the results.
In Comparison: If you're looking for a compact luxury SUV with a hybrid powertrain that's quicker in a straight line, check out the Volvo XC60 T8 PHEV, which raced to 60 mph in just 4.4 seconds.
Towing Capacity
- Max Towing: 3500 pounds
The Lexus RX Hybrid's max tow rating applies to all powertrains, and that figure is competitive with the rest of its classmates.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
- C/D Range Test: 30 miles
- EPA EV Range: 37 miles
The RX450h+ plug-in hybrid comes with an 18-kWh battery pack and a 6.6-kWh onboard AC charger. Lexus says it can be recharged in about two and a half hours on a 240-volt connection, and a full battery is said to offer up to 37 miles of electric-only driving, per the EPA. In our testing, the RX450h+ managed 30 miles of highway driving before the battery was depleted.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
- C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 28 mph (RX500h), 30 mpg (RX450h+)
- EPA City Ratings: 27–37 mpg
- EPA Highway Ratings: 28–38 mpg
The EPA's data shows that the most efficient RX model is the RX350h, which carries ratings of 37 mpg city and 34 mpg highway. The RX500h has estimates of 27 mpg city and 28 mpg highway, while the plug-in RX450h+ model is rated at 36 mpg city and 33 mpg highway.
On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy route, the RX500h F Sport Performance returned 28 mpg, matching its EPA estimate. The RX450h+ managed 30 mpg and 64 MPGe in our real-world test. For more information about the RX's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
In Comparison: The RX PHEV's real-world highway result is identical or very close to plug-in versions of the XC60 (30 mpg) and the Lincoln Corsair (31 mpg).
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
First Row: The RX Hybrid's interior design is modern and attractive, with textured fabric sections on the upper door panels, rich-looking ambient lighting, and open-pore wood trim on RX350h models. The RX500h F Sport Performance features more heavily bolstered front seats, black interior trim, steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters, and aluminum pedals.
Second Row: All RX Hybrids are two-row, five-seat affairs, with plentiful passenger space in both the front and rear seats. If you need a third row, consider the larger TX Hybrid.
Cargo Capacity: The cargo area is generously sized, too, and we managed to squeeze 11 carry-on suitcases behind the second row. The rear seats fold flat, and with them stowed, the RX offered space for 25 carry-ons in our testing.
Infotainment and Connectivity
- Infotainment: 9.8-inch touchscreen (standard), 14.0-inch touchscreen (optional)
- Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, available Wi-Fi hotspot
- Audio System: 12-speaker stereo (standard), 21-speaker Mark Levinson sound system (optional)
As in the smaller NX SUV, the RX's infotainment display is angled slightly toward the driver and uses Lexus's latest software interface. Wireless phone charging is standard, but features such as navigation, a head-up display, and a Mark Levinson stereo system are optional.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Overall Safety Rating (NHTSA)
Lexus offers many standard driver-assistance features on its new cars and SUVs, and the RX Hybrid is no different.
- Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control with lane centering
For information about the RX Hybrid's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Lexus's limited warranty matches most of its rivals in this segment. Its powertrain warranty surpasses many, and its hybrid components get longer coverage. However, complimentary scheduled maintenance lasts only one year, whereas the BMW X3 and the Volvo XC60 both offer lengthier terms.
- Limited Warranty: four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: six years or 70,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: one year or 10,00 miles

title: 2026 Volvo XC60 Hybrid Review, Pricing, and Specs
author: Andrew Wendler
text:
2026 Volvo XC60 Hybrid
Car and Driver
Accolades- Powerful and parsimonious powertrain, mild styling tweaks freshen the exterior, good balance of practicality and luxury.
- Ride can be harsh on broken pavement, slow at recharging.
- With a quick and efficient plug-in hybrid powertrain wrapped in Cool Swede style, the XC60 Hybrid makes for a sensible, tasteful choice that's now fully ripened.

Overview
Though the Volvo XC60 T8 Hybrid SUV is a near doppelganger for the standard XC60, it trades that version's powertrain for a powerful plug-in-hybrid system that not only increases efficiency but also brings some heat. Specifically, it offers an EPA-estimated 35 miles of electric-only range and up to 63 MPGe, all while laying down a 4.4-second leap to 60 mph in C/D testing. In nearly every other respect, the five-passenger XC60 Hybrid SUV is a virtual twin to its sibling: handsome Scandinavian exterior styling gives way to a comfortable and functional interior with a logical design, premium materials and finishes, and thoughtful touches. While the XC60 Hybrid is starting to show its age, Volvo gave it a few cosmetic tweaks to help it compete with the likes of the all-new Audi Q5 PHEV. If the XC60 Hybrid's Cool Swede style appeals to you, know that it remains a C/D favorite—as well as a sensible choice.
Where This Vehicle Ranks
#1 in Best Hybrid Compact Luxury SUVsCompare the 2026 Volvo XC60 Hybrid with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
What's New for 2026?
The 2026 XC60 Hybrid swaps a new 11.2-inch infotainment touchscreen in place of the outgoing 9.0-inch unit. Volvo claims better image quality and faster operating speed for all of its functions. Cosmetic tweaks include a new diagonal pattern for the grille and a subtle darkening of the taillight shroud. New wheel options are on the menu, as are a trio of paint colors including Forest Lake, Aurora Silver, and Mulberry Red.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
Pricing and Which One to Buy
Compare the 2026 Volvo XC60 Hybrid to other vehicles you're interested in
Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
Engine, Transmission, and Performance
The plug-in-hybrid XC60 T8 uses a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder paired with an electric motor powering the rear wheels. Additionally, a starter/generator motor mounted between the eight-speed automatic transmission and the gasoline engine can also charge the battery and add torque when needed. Total system output is 455 horsepower. The standard all-wheel drive and firmly compliant suspension provide a well-planted ride that can sometimes be a bit harsh over poor-quality roadway. Steering is precise but devoid of any nuance or feedback. Confidence is the key word here, not aggression. The top Polestar Engineered model offers sportier handling and the 21-inch wheels—the largest diameter wheels in the lineup.
What's Your Car Worth?
Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.
0–60-MPH Times
In our testing, a 2026 XC60 T8 hybrid got to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds. That's considerably quicker than the Mercedes-Benz GLC350e hybrid, which did it in 5.9 seconds.
Towing and Payload Capacity
The 2026 Volvo XC60 Hybrid is rated to tow a maximum of 3500 pounds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
The plug-in hybrid model comes with a 14.7-kWh battery pack that's good for an EPA-estimated 35 miles of electric driving per charge; we managed 31 miles in our testing. Recharging the battery is a time-consuming affair, due largely to the slow 3.7-kW max charge rate of the onboard charger. As such, it requires between five and eight hours to refill the battery, depending on the amperage of the Level 2 charging station.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG
The EPA estimates the Volvo XC60 T8 will return 28 mpg city and 28 mpg highway. With a fully charged battery, it earns an EPA rating of 63 MPGe. (A full explainer of MPGe can be found here.) In Car and Driver testing, the XC60 T8 returned 29 MPGe combined, and 30 mpg in our 75-mph real-world highway fuel-economy test. For more information about the T8's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
Even the base Core model looks upscale thanks to its adherence to Volvo's clean and logical design ethos. The tidy lines and high-quality interior materials add a distinctly Scandinavian flavor, and the cabin also provides adult-sized comfort in both rows. Cargo-hauling capability puts the XC60 mid-pack among its rivals in our testing with 22 cubic feet of cargo room behind the second row or 63 with it folded; with its rear seats down, we fit 20 of our carry-on suitcases.
Infotainment and Connectivity
All XC60 models come with a new 11.2-inch touchscreen infotainment display that runs Volvo's latest Google-based software interface, said to be up to twice as fast as the previous year's system. The system provides several personalization options and offers voice controls via Google Assistant. We've found the software interface to be quick to respond, but its menus require some familiarization and some of the icons are small. Redundant physical controls for volume and HVAC operation ease the strain. Standard audio is an 11-speaker setup, but a 14-speaker Harmon Kardon premium system is available on the Plus trim while a Bowers and Wilkens system is available on the Ultra and standard on the Polestar engineered. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are both standard, as is Bluetooth connectivity and an onboard Wi-Fi hotspot powered by a 4G LTE data connection.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Overall Safety Rating (NHTSA)
Volvo's commitment to safety is evident in the XC60, with driver-assistance features such as automated emergency braking and lane-keeping assist standard across the range. For more information about the XC60's crash test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Standard lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Available adaptive cruise control with semi-autonomous driving mode
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
Relative to its rivals in this segment, the XC60 has an appealing warranty policy. Three years of scheduled maintenance is a convenience that Volvo buyers won't need to pay for separately, either.
- Limited warranty covers 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Hybrid components are covered for 8 years or 100,000 miles
- Complimentary scheduled maintenance is covered for 3 years or 36,000 miles

title: You Have to Want a Plug-In Hybrid to Go for the Mercedes GLC350e
text:
Numbers don't lie, but the marketing associated with them often does. Going into this test of the 2025 GLC350e, we expected Mercedes's plug-in compact crossover to outperform its merely hybrid-assisted counterpart, the GLC300. But as is sometimes the case with plug-in-hybrid SUVs, the results weren't quite what we anticipated.
A Story in Two Parts
By superficial accounting, the GLC350e should have the edge here. Badge-wise, it has a 50-point advantage. Parsing their implied powertrain differences is less straightforward.
GLC300s use a turbocharged inline-four making 255 horsepower and 295 pound-feet of torque. The GLC350e gets a 201-hp version of that engine with 236 pound-feet, and it's aided by an electric motor good for 134 horsepower and a stout 325 pound-feet as long as there's juice in the 23.3-kWh battery pack; total system output is 313 horsepower and 406 pound-feet. But when you factor in the 48-volt hybrid-assist system's potential contribution in the GLC300—up to 23 horsepower and 148 pound-feet of torque—as well as the 740-pound weight penalty imposed by the 350e's battery pack, the bench race closes up.
For Sale Near You
See all results for new 2025 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class Hybrid for sale near 228211
For its part, Mercedes quotes identical 6.2-second zero-to-60-mph times for all non-AMG GLCs—the rear- and all-wheel-drive GLC300s, as well as the all-wheel-drive-only GLC350e. In our testing, a GLC300 4Matic reached 60 in 5.7 seconds. This GLC350e needed 5.9 seconds to do the same. By this metric, 350 is less than 300.
What the GLC300 can't do is a convincing impression of an electric vehicle. The GLC350e manages an EPA-estimated 54 miles when powered by electrons and can reach a max speed of 87 mph whole doing so. It defaults to electric driving, again as long as there's something left in the battery.
Characteristically Uncharacteristic Responses
When the charge runs out, though, another dichotomy rears its head. Without its e-parts pulling their weight, the GLC350e acts like what it is—a GLC300 that's down on power and carrying 700-plus pounds of ballast. We suppose this two-faced powertrain would encourage owners to keep their plug-in GLC charged up when not in use. It can recharge in a couple of hours on a Level 2 home charger so it's ready for the next day while you sleep, but it also can replenish its supply on a road trip in as little as a half hour at a max rate of 60 kilowatts on a fast-charger. We saw 30 MPGe over the course of our testing, which frankly indicates how little we plugged it in.
Bringing the GLC350e to a stop comes with the familiar unfamiliarity of other electrified Mercedes vehicles' brake pedals. Moving through its travel, your foot is met with a spongy region followed by some spring and finally a wooden response. There's a bit of a delay between applying pressure and getting the expected response, which is mildly disconcerting until you get used to it. You can prime the pump in a way by selecting D-, which provides maximum regeneration when you lift off the accelerator pedal; D Auto makes its own decisions but tries to coach you based on factors like the distance to the vehicle ahead, while D+ is akin to driving a regen-free gas-powered vehicle. We recorded a 172-foot stop from 70 mph with the PHEV, 11 feet longer than the GLC300 needed.

See all results for new 2025 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class Hybrid for sale near 228211
After a big whomp on the accelerator pedal, the 350e takes a beat to sort things out and deliver its full power. This could help explain its lack of performance compared to the GLC300. The steering is no different from that in other GLCs and Benzes in general; there's some buildup of weight off-center but not much in the way of feedback. It's comfort over confidence.
To counteract the added weight of the battery that lives under the cargo area, Mercedes fits the plug-in GLC with a self-leveling rear air suspension. The added cushion keeps the extra mass from calling attention to itself, but there's some clomp over big road imperfections, as there is in other GLCs. This unique suspension setup allows the driver to dial in more rear height when Off-Road mode is active, although we're not sure what kind of obstacles would be easier to clear with such a stance.
The Choice Under the Hood
Regardless of which GLC you're sitting in, you'll get the same experience. There's plenty of tech, including the touchy touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls and a big center display that features the third generation of MBUX infotainment software, new to the GLC lineup for 2025. The design is futuristic and tailored, and everything you touch has a nice feel to it, with a bit of heft to the controls.
Like the GLC300, the 350e is offered in three trims: Standard, Exclusive, and Pinnacle. Our test vehicle was a top-of-the-line Pinnacle model with a handful of additional options, including a leather-look dashboard, ventilation for the front seats, a panoramic sunroof, and the Driver Assistance package (adaptive cruise control and all manner of crash prevention and minimization). Its $61,050 base price is $8650 more than a GLC300 4Matic's.
As is the case with PHEVs in general, the payback in performance and efficiency only makes sense if you plan to exercise its electric range as often as possible, and with the GLC350e there's plenty to take advantage of. Just don't assume bigger numbers always win.
